ussr_kv_1_zis_5: A gun upgrade for the KV-1, this variant swaps the L-11 for the 76 mm ZiS-5, the weapon also carried by the T-34 (1942), while keeping the familiar heavy armour. The gun reloads briskly and does real damage once through, though its low muzzle velocity makes distant shots awkward and it leans on APCR for penetration. Angled, the hull is very hard to crack, helped by 25 mm of spaced plating on the front that takes it past 100 mm; the turret is the softer target, although its reinforced ring resists jamming. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_kv_1e: The 1940 "E" model of the KV-1 had extra steel plates riveted over its hull and turret and traded the old L-11 for the F-32, a gun close to the early T-34's; German units often had to bring in aircraft or towed 88 mm guns to stop one. In the game it combines tough armour with respectable mobility for a heavy tank, but the gun struggles to penetrate at range, so it does its best work pushing in close. It arrived as a premium pack in Update 1.41.27, left the store after the 2018 Winter sale and has since come back for Golden Eagles during Soviet-themed mini-events.
ussr_kv_1s: Built at Chelyabinsk in 1942 to answer crew complaints about the KV-1's sluggishness and unreliable parts, the KV-1S ("Skorostnoy", or "Speedy") was smaller, had thinner side armour and a new transmission; 1,086 were produced up to 1943. It can keep pace with medium tanks and reverses unusually fast for a Soviet design, and its 76 mm ZiS-5 has a varied ammunition choice including the BR-350B APCBC. The price is weaker protection, plus a slow turret and long reload that hurt it at close quarters. It was added in Update 1.57 "Battle March".
ussr_kv_220: An up-armoured member of the KV family with 100 mm of plate all round the hull and turret and an 85 mm gun, the KV-220 was a gift from the "Operation S.U.M.M.E.R." event in Update 1.61 "Road to Glory". Its even armour lets it angle freely without exposing a weak side, and it moves well for its weight, so it can brawl, support or snipe. The gun deals with mediums and early heavies but lacks the APCR and APHE options of the IS-1 and T-34-85, leaving it short against tanks like the M26. The mantlet is a shot trap that can deflect rounds into the 30 mm roof.
ussr_kv_2_1939: A KV-1 derivative carrying a 152 mm M-10T howitzer in a huge, heavy turret, the KV-2 was meant to break fortified positions for the infantry. Few were made, and most were lost to breakdowns rather than German guns, which at the time could not get through its armour. In the game the shell is devastating against nearly anything it hits, but the slow-turning turret and towering profile are just as serious liabilities. It has been available since the ground forces closed beta and is one of the best-known tanks in the Soviet tree, nicknamed the "King of Derp" by players.
ussr_kv_2_1940: This gift version of the KV-2 carries the same 152 mm howitzer in an outsized turret and was handed out in the 2016 WW2 Chronicles and 2017 Festive Quest events; it has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta. As with the regular KV-2, each shell hits extremely hard, but the turret turns slowly and the boxy silhouette is hard to hide. It can still do damage, yet most other Soviet vehicles now outperform it. Players know it by several nicknames, including "the barn", "the fridge" and "Tsar Bomba".
ussr_kv_2_zis_6: Fitted with the ZiS-6 gun in a tall, enlarged rectangular turret, this KV-2 offshoot first appeared as a premium pack in Update 1.59 "Flaming Arrows" and, after spells in and out of the store, became a permanent Golden Eagle purchase in 2024. Its shells fly faster and flatter than the howitzer KV-2s' and it reloads more quickly, with firepower likened to a small IS-2, and it carries a six-man crew. It keeps the family's slow turret, poor acceleration and weak reverse, so the lighter KV-85 at the same level is the nimbler and quicker-firing alternative.
ussr_kv_7_u13: Ordered by Stalin in November 1941 and ready by December, the KV-7 put a triple mount of one 76 mm and two 45 mm guns on a KV hull, meant to be fired together; salvo fire proved impractical and inaccurate, and the project was dropped in spring 1942, its lessons feeding into the SU-152. In the game the three barrels help cover aiming errors and the armour lets it soak up fire, but the 45 mm guns often fail to penetrate and the mount's traverse and elevation limits are tight. It was a reward in the 2024 Dreams Come True event.
ussr_kv_8: About 102 KV-8s were built in 1942-43 as flamethrower tanks to replace thin-skinned T-26-based types, with an ATO-41 flamethrower in place of the coaxial machine gun, which forced a switch from the 76.2 mm gun to a 45 mm one; they fought at Stalingrad. The game version, on the early KV chassis, keeps good armour and reasonable mobility for a heavy tank, but its 45 mm gun is weaker than the KV-1's, and open-topped vehicles are especially vulnerable to its flamethrower. It was a reward from the 2026 "Legend of Victory" event.
ussr_kv_85: A wartime stopgap, the KV-85 married a modified KV-1S hull to the IS-85 (IS-1) turret and 85 mm D-5T gun; 148 were built at Chelyabinsk from September to December 1943, dropping the radio operator to free space for ammunition. It handles much like the IS-1: quick to reload, aim and traverse, with a well-penetrating shell carrying good explosive filler. Its 75 mm front and 60 mm sides offer little against opponents of its rank, so careful positioning matters more than armour. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_m3c: Apart from its paintwork, the Soviet M3 Medium is essentially the American M3 Lee, the name coming from its Russian designation. It carries a 75 mm gun in a sponson on the right of the hull alongside a 37 mm gun in an offset turret topped by a machine-gun cupola, all on a tall body with a stepped two-plate front. It joined the game in Update 1.55 "Royal Armour" as a gift from the February 2016 "Defender combined battles" event and has resurfaced since through Tanker's Day events and the Warbonds shop.
ussr_m4a2_76w_sherman: Of the 4,102 Shermans sent to the Soviet Union, 2,095 were 76 mm-armed M4A2 (76) W tanks, the first arriving in late summer 1944; crews valued their reliability, easy upkeep and firepower but disliked the tall silhouette and narrow tracks in mud. In the game its main asset is gun depression far better than native Soviet tanks have, which suits hull-down positions. The high profile is hard to conceal, so its good mobility is best spent reaching a firing spot before the enemy arrives. It came as a premium in Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
ussr_m53_59: The Czechoslovak M53/59 "Ještěrka" ("Lizard") mounts twin 30 mm ZK453 autocannons on a Praga V3S truck chassis; it never fought at home but saw combat in southern Europe and Africa. In the Soviet tree it doubles the firepower of comparable domestic anti-aircraft vehicles, with a high rate of fire and enough penetration to tear into light armour or tanks that expose their sides. Each load holds only 100 rounds in two 50-round magazines and reloading is slow, so ammunition must be rationed, especially against anything with heavy machine guns or HE. It arrived in the "Sky Guardians" update.
ussr_m53_59_kit_4rank: This version of the Czechoslovak twin-30 mm M53/59 truck SPAA, added in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey", wears camouflage drawn from Soviet Great Patriotic War vehicles. Its rapid twin guns shred aircraft and light armour in brief bursts, and in practised hands threaten medium and heavy tanks too. Because the cab sits low, the guns can also shoot straight ahead over it, which is unusual among truck-mounted AA. Quick on roads, it can dash to capture points or slip round a flank before the enemy reacts.
ussr_object_120: Developed in the 1960s when Soviet planners doubted the T-54/55 and T-10 could cope with new enemy tanks, the Object 120 carried a 152 mm gun firing APFSDS and HEAT-FS, but it was not adopted once smoothbore guns and portable missiles matched its penetration. In the game it is all firepower and almost no protection: the very long gun outclasses nearly everything nearby, while its armour is so thin that even small autocannons on tanks or aircraft can destroy it. It was added in Update 1.71 "New E.R.A.".
ussr_object_140: Designed at Nizhny Tagil in the 1950s under L.N. Kartsev as an improved T-54, the Object 140 had the stronger D-54TS gun, a rounder turret and aluminium road wheels; two were built by 1958 before its cramped, hard-to-service engine and transmission ended the project. In the game its APHE defeats any opponent frontally at close range, and an optical rangefinder makes it a capable sniper, backed by a KPVT for light vehicles. Drawbacks are poor gun depression, armour that only stops APHE, ammunition around the crew unless the load is kept light, and an 8 km/h reverse. It came in the "Firebirds" update.
ussr_object_248: Tested in late 1944, the Object 248 was an attempt to give the IS-1 a 100 mm S-34 gun (a sister design, the Object 245, used the D-10). Weak gun cradles and a breech that could strike the commander dogged trials, and by the time they were fixed newer designs had overtaken it, so it was cancelled. In the game its 100 mm reloads in under half the time of the IS-2's 122 mm and penetrates more at the cost of explosive filler, so it can play aggressively yet still hit at range. It was the Battle Pass Season VIII "Field Testing" reward in the "Danger Zone" update.
ussr_object_268: Built on the T-10 chassis as a successor to the ISU-152, the Object 268 was finished in 1956; its M-64 was among the first Soviet guns with a muzzle brake, but the design could not deal with the Chieftain or M60, so only one prototype was made. In the game it is a long-range support vehicle: the gun is strong and the rangefinder helps, but the hull is big and its thick armour belongs to an earlier era, so it should stay out of close fighting. It arrived in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
ussr_object_279: The Kirov Plant's SKB-2 in Leningrad, under L.S. Troyanov, built the Object 279 for a 1955 competition to replace the T-10, giving it four tracks, a cast hull shaped to resist a nuclear blast wave, thin skirts and an autoloader. The single prototype was completed in late 1959, but Khrushchev's 1960 ban on tanks over 37 tons ended the programme. In the game its large hull is easy to spot and newer tanks' APFSDS can get through, but against most other ammunition the armour holds up very well, the APC shell is strong and it moves respectably. It was the reward for the 2020 "Space Race" event.
ussr_object_292: An ambitious late-Soviet testbed, the Object 292 mounted a 152 mm smoothbore in a turret blending T-80BV and T-80U features, aiming to defeat NATO tanks at maximum range; the gun performed in trials but money ran out and the prototype was shelved. In the game it looks like a T-80U stripped of ERA and its anti-aircraft machine gun. Protection is only average, but the huge gun's penetration and damage can often knock out a target in one hit, though it cannot afford to waste a shot. It was a reward from the 2024 Call of the Dragon event in the "Air Superiority" update.
ussr_object_416: Kharkov Plant No. 75 designed the Object 416 in 1950 as a low light tank with its turret at the back; by the 1951 prototype it had become the SU-100M self-propelled gun, and trials found the driver's turret position, a cramped interior and no real edge over the SU-100P, so it was cancelled in 1953. In the game, putting the whole crew in the turret gives it a very low silhouette, and its gun is strong, but each reload takes a while, a hit tends to be costly and the gun can barely elevate or depress. It was added in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
ussr_object_435: Developed as a possible T-54/55 successor, the Object 435 combined an IS-style angular hull front, a T-62-like round turret and running gear foreshadowing the T-64, armed with the 115 mm U-5TS smoothbore; it lost out to the T-64 line and now sits in the Kubinka museum. In the game it plays much like a T-62, with strong APFSDS but a slow reload, slightly better mobility and turret traverse, and an optical rangefinder in place of the ESS. Unlike the T-62 it also carries a 14.5 mm KPVT heavy machine gun, handy against light vehicles and helicopters. It arrived in the "La Royale" update.
ussr_object_685: Drawn up as a replacement for the PT-76, the Object 685 had to stay under 15 tons while carrying a rifled 100 mm gun, a 9K111 Fagot missile system and a 12.7 mm machine gun, with anti-nuclear sealing and armour against 23 mm AP; it passed initial evaluation but never entered production, although later Soviet designs reused its components. In the game it is a quick flanker that accelerates well going forwards, reloads in 6 seconds and has an adequate 3BM25 dart. It pays for this with fragile protection, no thermal imaging and little gun depression. It was added in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
ussr_object_775: A mid-1960s Soviet missile tank destroyer, the Object 775 got its extremely low profile from a drum autoloader, a shortened gun-launcher and hydropneumatic suspension; trouble packing those systems into so small a hull, plus shifting doctrine, ended it in favour of the work that led to the T-64. In the game it excels at hidden strikes with a strong ATGM, a tiny silhouette and decent frontal armour, and its suspension and dozer blade let it dig in and rise only to fire. Weak sides, a two-man turret and ammunition lining the interior mean almost any penetration destroys it. It arrived in the "Kings of Battle" update.
ussr_object_906: The Object 906 was an 85 mm-armed development of the amphibious PT-76B that would have entered service as the PT-85, but it was judged too complex to build and run in quantity, so the PT-76 stayed. In the game it plays as a typical light tank: quick, low and lightly armoured, with no rangefinder. Its standout feature is a two-plane stabiliser that works at any speed, which makes ambushing light tanks rushing capture points straightforward. Gun depression is poor, as on many Soviet tanks, and it can swim when needed. It arrived in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
ussr_pantsyr_s1: Developed from the early 1990s by KBP Tula and the Ulyanovsk Mechanical Plant, the Pantsir-S1 covers short and medium distances, pairing advanced radar with both missiles and guns, and is heavily automated for fast reactions. Added in the "Sky Guardians" update as a top-tier SPAA, it is most effective against aircraft and helicopters at medium and close range, using missiles and autocannons together. Its thin armour leaves it exposed to ground threats, but good mobility and flexibility let it keep pace with the team as air cover.
ussr_pantsyr_sm_sv: The Pantsir-SM-SV puts the modernised Pantsir-SM combat module, with longer detection and engagement ranges and support for the small TKB-1055 missile, on a tracked chassis; a single tracked prototype went to the army, and troop trials have run since 2024. Compared with earlier Pantsirs it reaches much further against aircraft and moves better on its tracks, and four TKB-1055s can replace a single 95Ya6M, giving plenty of shots for intercepting incoming munitions. Its weakness is guidance: the target has to stay in line of sight, and attackers from opposite directions cannot both be handled at once. It arrived in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
ussr_pt_76_57: Also called the PT-76E, the PT-76-57 is the latest upgrade of the PT-76, with a BM-57 turret carrying the 57 mm AU-220M autocannon, night vision, a new stabiliser, a stronger engine and modern optics; 50 have been ordered. In the game it shares its BR-281 ammunition with the ZSU-57-2 but fires one barrel much faster, shredding IFVs and light tanks and punishing heavier tanks from the flank. Its APHE can even work frontally against lower-ranked opponents, and the laser rangefinder makes longer shots easy. It was the Battle Pass Season V "River Hunter" reward in the "Direct Hit" update.
ussr_pt_76b: The PT-76, designed by Nikolay Shashmurin and Joseph Kotin and in production from 1951, was a Soviet amphibious reconnaissance tank; the B model, made between 1959 and 1961, added a two-plane stabiliser, extra fuel and night vision. In the game it brings Cold War equipment into WWII-era matches: a HEATFS round that penetrates almost anything, the stabiliser and night vision, plus the ability to cross water. Its armour can be holed by machine guns and it is slow for a light tank, so it is best used as a scout and support gun. It arrived in Update 1.53 "Fire Storm", with swimming added in 1.55.
ussr_pzkpfw_III_ausf_J_L42: Captured Panzer IIIs were repaired and put into Red Army service as the T-III until 1943, when poor penetration and scarce captured ammunition led to their withdrawal; one damaged example had already been taken home secretly for study after the Polish campaign. In the game it is a Pz.III J with a capable 50 mm gun and good mobility, able to support light tanks and reach strong firing positions. The tightly packed crew and easily penetrated upper glacis and sides make it fragile, so angling the hull helps. It was added in Update 1.43.
ussr_pzkpfw_V: The Soviet T-V is a Panther Ausf. A in Red Army colours, given away during the 2015 Thunder League eSports tournament, first to Twitch viewers and then to every Dog-Tag holder once the prize pool reached $50,000. It shares the Panther's broad sloped glacis, curved mantlet and automotive performance, which makes it a dangerous opponent, but unlike the German original it has no APCR in its ammunition choice.
ussr_rbt_5: The RBT-5 was a BT-5 carrying two huge 420 mm TT-250 "tank torpedo" rockets meant for forts and heavy tanks; 1932 trials found them inaccurate and unstable, the weight also slowed the tank, and only a few prototypes existed when it was abandoned in 1933. In the game a light 11.5-ton hull, strong engine and Christie suspension make it fast and agile but almost unarmoured, and its 45 mm 20-K reloads quickly. The turret-side rockets are not lined up with the gun and need careful aim; the left fires first. Once a 2015 Thunder League prize, it is now available solely through the War Thunder Market.
ussr_sdkfz_251_21_kit_3rank: "Hanomag" was the Soviet nickname, taken from its maker, for the German Sd.Kfz.251 half-track; over 15,000 of all versions were built, and captured ones served with Soviet and Allied forces. This is the 251/21 anti-aircraft model, with three 20 mm MG 151/20 cannons, painted with the red stars and identification stripes Soviet vehicles carried during the Berlin operation. The triple mount has enough firepower for any aircraft and it handles rough ground well, but the armour is weak, the crew sits in an open compartment and reloads take a long time. It arrived in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
ussr_smk: Named after Sergei Kirov, the SMK was Josef Kotin's 1939 twin-turret heavy tank prototype meant to replace the T-35; trialled in the Winter War, it proved awkward in Finnish forests, was stranded for two months after hitting a mine, and lost out to the single-turret KV. In the game it is essentially a longer KV-1 with a second turret, but its sides, rear and turret are thinner. The length makes town fighting and peeking round corners difficult, the main turret's exposed neck is a weak spot, and with the crew packed tightly any penetration can be fatal. It arrived in Update 1.45 "Steel Generals" as a Golden Eagle premium.
ussr_su_100Y: Derived from the T-100 heavy tank prototype during the Winter War, the SU-100Y carried a 130 mm naval gun to blast fortifications for the infantry, much as the KV-2 did; the lone prototype is said to have fought near Moscow in 1941 and survives at Kubinka. In the game the B-13 fires SAPCBC with plenty of explosive filler and strong penetration even at long range, so few tanks survive a hit. The front armour is mediocre and easily defeated up close, and although it accelerates fairly well for its size, it reverses very slowly. It was added in Update 1.51 "Cold Steel".
ussr_su_100_1945: Designed in 1944 by L.I. Gorlitskiy's team at UZTM in Yekaterinburg, the SU-100 put a 100 mm D-10S on the T-34-85 chassis to defeat German heavy tanks at long range, and served widely in the war's last year and afterwards with Soviet allies. In the game it is a classic casemate tank destroyer with a fixed forward gun, suited to a defensive, supporting role: ambushing and engaging distant targets rather than meeting them head-on. Outwardly it differs little from the SU-85, yet the 100 mm is a major step up in firepower. It has been in the game since ground forces opened in Update 1.41.
ussr_su_100p: Also designated Object 105, the SU-100P was a prototype self-propelled gun developed alongside its rival, the Object 416, armed with the D-50, a higher-velocity derivative of the D-10 built specifically for it. Testing exposed an unreliable gun, chassis and lifting gear, and although it was improving, Khrushchev's dismissal of self-propelled guns ended the project; its chassis went on to underpin many other designs. In the game it works as a sniper like most Soviet tank destroyers, but its mobility also lets it reach awkward spots and flank, backed by an accurate, hard-hitting 100 mm gun. It was added in Update 1.71 "New E.R.A.".
ussr_su_122: Inspired by the success of the German StuG III, the SU-122 was a WWII assault gun that put a 122 mm M-30S howitzer on the T-34 chassis, a turretless layout that was cheaper to build and left room for a bigger gun. In the game its shell is formidable and the front armour turns away most rounds at its rank, but the reload is very long, so missed shots are costly. Heavy shell drop makes distant targets hard to hit, which makes it a vehicle for experienced players. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_su_122P: With D-10S gun production running late in 1944, L.I. Gorlitsky's UZTM team fitted a 122 mm D-25S into a spare SU-100 hull as a stopgap; in autumn trials it proved slower-firing, carried fewer rounds and was less comfortable for its crew than the SU-100, so only the prototype was built. In the game it pairs excellent firepower with good mobility, and a single shot destroys most targets. The armour is thin and crew and ammunition are crammed together, so it is fragile, but its small size suits ambushes and fighting from the second line.
ussr_su_122_54: Plant No. 174 developed the SU-122-54 between 1948 and 1951 on T-54 running gear to replace wartime self-propelled guns; after two prototypes and state trials it entered production, but only 77 were built from 1955 to 1957 before gun-material shortages and newer projects stopped it, and it served until the mid-1960s. In the game its strong gun and low, compact hull make it easy to hide and hard to spot. The reload is long, even ordinary AP can get through the front, and mobility is average, so it does best ambushing or sniping from range. It arrived in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
ussr_su_152: Operation Uranus at Stalingrad showed the Red Army needed mobile heavy guns to crack fortifications, and the SU-152 answered by mounting a 152 mm ML-20S howitzer on the KV-1S chassis; its ability to knock out heavy German armour earned it the name Zveroboy, "beast slayer". In the game it is a flexible tank destroyer: armour-piercing rounds are the main choice against the heavily armoured enemies it meets, while HE still works well on light vehicles. The very long reload means each shot must be chosen carefully. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_su_57: SU-57 was the Soviet name for the American T48 GMC, a Diamond T half-track carrying a US-built version of the British 57 mm six-pounder; of 962 built in 1942-43, 650 went to the USSR under Lend-Lease after the British and Americans found little use for them. In the game it resembles the 75 mm GMC M3, and its accurate, quick-firing 57 mm M1 penetrates well enough to make it an effective long-range tank destroyer. It is fast and agile, which it needs, because its armour offers almost no protection: fire from distance, then relocate before the enemy replies. It was added in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
ussr_su_57b: Armed with the 57 mm ZiS-4, a gun with excellent penetration for its rank, the SU-57B is a low-slung Soviet tank destroyer. Its small profile lets it creep up behind bushes and terrain to ambush unaware enemies from medium range, but its armour is weak from every angle. It can reach 40 km/h in Realistic Battles, yet overall it is less nimble than the ZiS-30, which relocates faster, so it only performs well when it stays well placed and unseen. It was added in Update 1.83 "Masters of the Sea".
ussr_su_5_1: Built in 1934 for the "small triplex" programme of artillery mounts on a common T-26 (1933) chassis, the SU-5-1 was the lightest of the three, carrying a 76 mm 1902/30 divisional gun; it tested poorly, was superseded by the AT-1, and only one was made. In the game its gun is exceptionally strong for its rank, able to kill in one hit even at range, but survivability is very low and ammunition scarce. The T-26 chassis reaches most positions, the tall gun shield tends to draw shots that pass over the crew, and APHE striking the body may pass straight through without detonating. It arrived in Update 1.67 "Assault".
ussr_su_76d: A proposed light tank destroyer on the T-70 chassis, the SU-76D (no relation to the SU-76M) took its "D" from a 110 hp diesel engine; its 76.2 mm gun could no longer penetrate newer German tanks, the engine was underpowered and hard to tune, and the project was dropped. In the game it is small and light, but its armour is thin and its mobility only average. The BR-350B shell penetrates and wrecks most opponents it meets, so it rewards a stealthy approach. It was the Future Technology event reward in the "Ixwa Strike" update.
ussr_su_76m_1943: The SU-76 was the Red Army's most numerous self-propelled gun, an infantry-support vehicle on T-60/T-70 running gear; the 1943 SU-76M added an open fighting compartment and a longer-lasting engine, and over 14,000 were built by 1945, later serving with Poland, China, North Korea and others. In the game its 76 mm gun handles most opponents out to about 1 km, making it a decent sniper. Thin armour and the open top mean it should usually fight from cover at range, though a skilled crew can support allies closer in. Being compact and nimble helps it stay unnoticed. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_su_76m_5st_kav_corps: This gift version of the small open-topped SU-76M was introduced in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory" and handed out in WW2 Chronicles and Tanker's Day events in 2015 and 2017, then via a Warbonds trophy chest in 2018. Its 76.2 mm ZiS-3 fires quickly and can penetrate any opponent it meets from the front, and the shrapnel shell is so effective against SPAA and other light vehicles that HE is barely needed. In return it is a nimble but fragile target with very little protection.
ussr_su_85_1943: When German tanks outgrew existing Soviet guns, Petrov's bureau produced the 85 mm D-5 in May 1943; too large for the tanks then in service, it went into a modified SU-122 on the T-34 chassis as the D-5S, creating the SU-85. In the game the gun can destroy most tanks of its rank, but the armour stops very little, so it belongs well behind the front, using range and its low silhouette to stay hidden while picking targets off. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_su_85a: Built for trials in late 1943 as a possible successor to the SU-76M, the SU-85A swapped the older 76 mm gun for a modified 85 mm anti-aircraft cannon, but poor mechanical performance meant it never progressed beyond testing. It came to the game in Update 1.85 "Supersonic" as a gift vehicle from the 2018 Festive Quest event.
ussr_su_85m: The SU-85M was a refined SU-85 rather than a new variant, with slightly thicker frontal armour and an improved commander's cupola; 315 were built. In the game the powerful gun makes it a long-range sniper, and the lack of a turret rules out close fighting despite the extra front armour, which barely matters against the stronger opponents it faces. It works best hanging back behind the main fight, using distance and its low profile to survive while picking off targets. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_t_10a: An early-1950s development of the IS line, the T-10A improved on the IS-3 with better armour, a stronger engine and more firepower, adding a vertical stabiliser and a turret layout that made reloading easier; it was soon followed by the more substantial T-10B and T-10M. In the game it is the first Soviet heavy tank with a one-plane stabiliser, which makes firing on the move far easier. Its armour is unreliable against HEATFS and APDS, but the 122 mm D-25TS reloads considerably faster than the D-25T of earlier IS tanks. It was the Battle Pass Season I reward in the "New Power" update.
ussr_t_10m: The T-10M was the final form of the T-10 (Object 730, meant to be the IS-8 until Stalin's death prompted a rename): it gained a fully automatic two-plane stabiliser, infrared night vision, NBC protection and a 14.5 mm KPVT, plus a longer 122 mm M-62-T2S with a multi-baffle muzzle brake. No later IS-family tank entered Soviet service, and the T-64 soon pushed it out of front-line units. In the game it beats its predecessors in firepower, armour and speed, handling like a slightly sluggish medium tank with a 40 km/h top speed; the slow reload is its main drawback. It arrived in Update 1.51 "Cold Steel".
ussr_t_126sp: The T-126 was the prototype that led to the T-50 light tank; two were built, with a differently shaped hull carrying 55 mm at the front and 45 mm sides, and a turret without a cupola armoured to 45 mm all round. In the game it is effectively a premium T-50 with noticeably thicker armour, which costs it some top speed, although it remains fairly mobile. It was introduced as a Golden Eagle premium in Update 1.47 "Big Guns".
ussr_t_26E: Drawing on Winter War experience, Leningrad Factory No. 174 bolted and welded extra plates onto 89 T-26s to make the T-26E ("ekranirovanny", screened), bringing protection to 45 mm all round; factory tests showed it could resist 45 mm anti-tank guns at 400 to 500 m. In the game, correct angling gives it a fair chance of bouncing shells off the front, but the extra weight makes already modest mobility worse. It was a premium pack from the ground forces closed beta, was taken off sale after Victory Day 2017 and later returned through Warbonds and Battle Pass trophies.
ussr_t_26_1940: Based on the British Vickers 6-ton tank, the T-26 was the Red Army's main light tank of the 1930s, fighting in Spain and Finland and suffering heavy losses against Panzer IIIs and IVs in 1941; around 12,000 of all variants were built between 1931 and 1941. In the game its 45 mm APHE has the penetration and filler to knock out most opponents in one shot, making up for a small, thinly armoured hull. Mobility is poor, behind the Panzer II and every BT, and gun depression is limited, as on other Soviet tanks. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_t_26_1940_1st_GvTBr: Some T-26s served with the 1st Guards Tank Brigade, the "Katukov Brigade", which fought from Moscow and Kursk to the edge of Berlin, and this version wears that unit's distinctive camouflage. The T-26 itself was a Vickers 6-ton derivative, with 11,218 built. In the game it plays almost like a self-propelled gun: slow, fragile and hard to spot, but able to hurt the enemy from cover and at distance. For newer players it offers a strong gun while its thin armour and limited mobility teach careful positioning. It was added in Update 1.41.27.12.
ussr_t_26_4: Also known as the T-26A, the T-26-4 was a close-support version of the T-26 with an enlarged A-43 turret holding the 76 mm KT-28 howitzer used on early T-28s and T-35s; tested from 1932 to 1934, it disappointed and only five were built. In the game it is a specialist and demanding vehicle, since the howitzer's looping trajectory and low penetration call for a quite different approach from the standard T-26's 45 mm. Weak armour and poor mobility add to the challenge, though it remains effective against lightly armoured targets. It was introduced in Update 1.51 "Cold Steel".
ussr_t_28: Developed in the early 1930s alongside the T-35, with which it shared hull and turret designs, the three-turreted T-28 carried a 76 mm L-10 howitzer and DT machine guns for infantry support; after the Winter and Continuation Wars its front was up-armoured to 80 mm, and it fought around Leningrad and Moscow in 1941 before being retired. In the game the stock shrapnel and HE are nearly useless against armour, so the BR-350A APHEBC is the priority research. It moves well for its size and reaches 40 km/h, but the armour is modest and the six crew are packed so tightly that one good shot can destroy it.
ussr_t_28E: The T-28E ("ekranirovanny", shielded) was the T-28 with extra plates welded over its armour after the Winter War, which pushed its weight from 28 to 32 tons. In the game it plays just like the regular T-28, only with thicker plating all round, which helps it last longer in both close brawls and long-range duels. The extra weight costs it a little manoeuvrability compared with the standard model. It was introduced in Update 1.47 "Big Guns".
ussr_t_28_1938: This early production T-28 has the three-turret layout of the infantry-support tank designed alongside the T-35, but its main turret carries the 76 mm KT-28 howitzer rather than the L-10 of later versions. In the game that howitzer's APHEBC penetrates just 34 mm at 500 m, so armoured targets are a struggle. It is fairly mobile for its bulk with a 40 km/h top speed, but thin armour and six tightly packed crew mean a single well-placed hit can finish it. It was added in the "Ixwa Strike" update.
ussr_t_34E: The T-34E is a T-34 carrying 16 mm spaced plates on the turret and hull sides, extra layers that can turn shells aside when the tank is angled well, and in practice it often does better than standard T-34s. It was sold as a premium pack from Update 1.41 in June 2014 until October 2016, stayed on Steam until August 2018, and then became a reward in the 2018 "Operation S.U.M.M.E.R." crafting event.
ussr_t_34E_STZ: To keep up with improving German guns, the Stalingrad Tractor Factory (STZ) welded extra plates onto the front of T-34 (1941) tanks, mostly in January 1942; the "E" stands for "ehkranami", screened. In the game it is a T-34 (1941) with a thicker front hull and nothing else changed, keeping the long 76.2 mm F-34 and its broad ammunition choice. The added protection makes head-on fights noticeably safer, at the cost of some speed. It arrived in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
ussr_t_34_100: The last development of the T-34, begun in July 1944 because the T-34's guns were failing against the latest German armour, the T-34-100 paired a 100 mm LB-1 gun with a T-44V turret and a reworked interior. It was finished in the first half of 1945 but never mass-produced, as the superior T-44 was close to completion. In the game its weak armour and poor reverse speed make it a poor spearhead, and it does better backing the team up from behind. It was added in Update 1.51 "Cold Steel".
ussr_t_34_1940_l_11: The A-34, designed at Kharkiv Factory No. 183 under Mikhail Koshkin between 1937 and 1939, grew out of the BT-7M with a welded hull, 45 mm sloped front armour and a 76 mm L-11 gun, and was adopted as the T-34 in December 1939. In the game it shares the family's speed, gun and sloped plate, so it suits flanking and brawling, though the turret cheeks, front hull step, machine-gun port and turret ring are weak spots. It was a pre-order exclusive during the ground forces closed beta, with 500 more sold during the 5th Anniversary event.
ussr_t_34_1941: The second production T-34 brought the long 76.2 mm F-34 gun and a welded turret with a single large hatch; crews disliked the heavy, jam-prone hatch, nicknamed the "pirozhok" (stuffed bun), and the turret had no rotating periscope. In the game it is the T-34 (1940) with much better firepower: the longer barrel's higher velocity makes hitting targets easier, and improved ammunition helps further. Sloped frontal armour, strong off-road performance and agility round out a well-balanced medium tank. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_t_34_1941_57: In 1941 V.G. Grabin's 57 mm ZiS-4, a tank version of the ZiS-2, was fitted to a T-34 (1941); approved for production in July, only 10 were built before it was halted in September for lack of resources and AP ammunition, and it was later nicknamed "Exterminator". In the game it out-penetrates every other early T-34 and fights well at long range, but the small shell does little damage inside, so kills may take several hits. With armour that stops little, it relies on speed and moving between cover. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_t_34_1941_cast_turret: This premium T-34 (1941) wears the markings of the 1st Guards Tank Brigade, which began as the 4th Tank Brigade and, after fighting in the Battle of Moscow, became the Red Army's very first Guards tank brigade. It differs from the standard tank in having a cast rather than rolled turret, and otherwise plays almost identically. Added in Update 1.41, it was sold as a pack until the 2018 Winter sale and has since returned for Golden Eagles during several Soviet-themed mini-events.
ussr_t_34_1941_l_11: The first mass-produced T-34 traced its design to the 1938 A-32, itself drawing on the Christie-based BT-7M; early examples suffered from a hard-to-build hull front, a shortage of V12 diesels that left many with the weaker M-17 engine, and a low-velocity 76 mm L-11. More than 84,000 T-34s of all types were eventually built. In the game its 45 mm frontal plate is sloped enough to resist most guns at range, and it crosses mud and soft ground easily, which helps it seize ground early. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_t_34_1942: By 1942 the T-34 was being simplified for mass production: the F-34 gun's part count fell from 861 to 614, rubber shortages led to mixed metal road wheels, and a new hexagonal turret with twin hatches, which Germans nicknamed "Mickey Mouse", replaced the single-hatch design. In the game it is close to the T-34 (1941) but reloads a little faster, has a thicker driver's hatch and gets APCR. As opponents' guns grow stronger, though, the frontal hull plate increasingly fails to stop them. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_t_34_57_1943: The 57 mm T-34 idea was revived in 1943, this time with the improved ZiS-4M in a hexagonal-turret T-34 (1943); it went to the front with Special Tank Company 100 in August 1943 but never fought, and the arrival of the 85 mm D-5 ended the 57 mm effort. In the game this premium plays like the earlier T-34-57 with the newer gun and APCR for tougher targets, though the small calibre often needs several hits to finish a tank. It looks like the T-34 (1942) thanks to the same turret, and has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_t_34_85E: The T-34-85, the Red Army's answer to the Tiger and Panther, added the 85 mm ZiS-S-53 and a roomier turret with a cupola and a dedicated loader; this one carries field-fitted mesh screens against the German shaped-charge infantry weapons met on the way to Berlin. In the game the loader gives it a quicker reload than the T-34-85 (D-5T), and with APCR it is very effective on flanking runs, though weak optics and long-range ballistics make it a poor sniper. Functionally it matches the T-34-85 ('45). Added as a premium in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory", it is now sold only in the "Tracks of Victory" bundle.
ussr_t_34_85_d_5t: The first T-34-85 in the game pairs a new, stronger turret with the 85 mm D-5T, a gun later replaced in production by the improved ZiS-S-53. Otherwise it is very much a T-34, keeping the family's strengths and weaknesses, so experienced T-34 drivers adapt quickly, and so do their opponents. Its speed and effective gun make it good at reaching capture points early and holding them until heavier allies arrive. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_t_34_85_stp_s53: Soviet engineers trialled stabilisers on T-34s from 1943, and in 1945 five T-34-85s were built with the STP-S-53 system; 1946 trials found accuracy on the move at up to 25 km/h improved two-and-a-half to three times, but the 85 mm gun and T-34 platform were by then obsolete and the programme ended. In the game it is a standard T-34-85 apart from its single-plane stabiliser, which makes firing on the move far more practical. Frontal penetration is unreliable but damage after penetration is strong, while the armour is weak and depends largely on lucky ricochets. It arrived in Update 2.51 "Spearhead".
ussr_t_34_85_zis_53: This T-34-85 replaces the D-5T of the earlier model with the improved 85 mm ZiS-S-53 and adds a fifth crewman, giving it a quicker reload and APCR, while the rest of the specification is unchanged. Its 45 mm front plate, though sloped, is defeated by virtually every gun it meets, so the hull is best kept out of enemy sight lines whenever possible. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_t_34_85_zis_53_kit_3rank: The T-34-85 entered service in spring 1944 to counter the Panther and Tiger; late in the war some crews added improvised screens to the hull and turret sides against Panzerfaust-armed infantry in city fighting, though the practice was rare and of doubtful value. This version carries those screens plus the identification stripes of the Berlin operation, resembling the T-34-85E. It is still quick and thinly armoured, with an accurate 85 mm gun that can defeat almost any tank at its rank when aimed carefully. It was added in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
ussr_t_34_85_zis_53_v80: "Partisan", tactical number 3-716, was a T-34-85 of the 61st Guards Sverdlovsk-Lvov Tank Brigade, part of the 10th Guards Ural Volunteer Tank Corps, which fought through the 1944-45 Lvov-Sandomierz, Berlin and Prague offensives and earned many high honours. The in-game version, from the 2025 "Legend of Victory" event, adds red-banner decoration and unique insignia to a standard T-34-85. It plays as usual: fast and lightly armoured, with an accurate 85 mm gun that can deal with nearly every tank it meets.
ussr_t_35: The world's only five-turreted tank, the T-35 was in effect a scaled-up T-28 crewed by ten; just 59 were built between 1934 and 1939, dogged by a weak engine, cramped compartments and no more than 30 mm of armour. In the game the large crew lets it survive hits that would kill other tanks, but the main KT-28 howitzer struggles to penetrate, so the 45 mm 20-K in a forward turret, good for up to 58 mm, is the better weapon. Heavy machine-gun fire can get through its thin plates, and it tops out at 28 km/h. It was added in Update 1.43.
ussr_t_44: Design Bureau No. 183 developed the T-44 in 1943-44 to give Soviet crews better armour than the T-34 against Panthers and Tigers; 1,823 were built up to 1947, but its only combat came in the suppression of the Hungarian Uprising, and it paved the way for the T-54. In the game its good frontal armour and low profile give it fair protection, and quick turret traverse and decent reverse suit close-range and urban fighting. The gun struggles with some heavily armoured targets, and the compact layout means one penetrating shell often destroys it. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_t_44_100: After 122 mm trials on the T-44 disappointed, a 100 mm D-10T version was tested from October 1944 with an enlarged turret ring, thicker turret armour and side panels; it performed well, but only two prototypes were built before the army moved to a more modern design, the T-54. In the game it is fast and low, and its 100 mm rivals the Tiger II's 88 mm in velocity and explosive filler, though it reloads slowly. With thin armour and poor gun depression it works better flanking and ambushing than holding a line, using a quick reverse to shoot and scoot. It arrived in Update 1.57 "Battle March".
ussr_t_44_122: The third T-44 prototype carried a 122 mm D-25-44T firing single-piece ammunition; 1944 trials against a captured Panther and an 85 mm T-44 showed a rate of fire of only two or three rounds a minute and stowage for just 24 rounds, so work continued on the 85 mm version instead. In the game the 122 mm gives a huge jump in firepower over the 85 mm T-44, and mobility and armour are excellent, though a protruding, partly flat driver's hatch is a weak spot. It can snipe or brawl, ducking into cover while reloading. It was a Golden Eagle premium in Update 1.55 "Royal Armour".
ussr_t_44_kit_4rank: This T-44 wears camouflage modelled on Soviet tanks of the Great Patriotic War and was added in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey". The T-44 itself was Design Bureau No. 183's 1943-44 attempt to out-armour the T-34; 1,823 were made, seeing combat only against the Hungarian Uprising. As on the standard model, its strong front and low silhouette give reasonable protection, and a fast turret and good reverse help in close or urban fighting. Some heavily armoured targets are beyond its gun, and one penetrating hit often wipes out the cramped crew.
ussr_t_44_po: The first-model T-44 was a clean-sheet design after the T-43 failed to replace the T-34, with a transverse engine to make room for a central turret and thicker front armour; the January 1944 prototype showed promise, but its driver's position and high turret ring hurt protection, and refinements led to the final T-44. In the game its gun has modest penetration, so weak spots need targeting, yet the large explosive charge often destroys a tank in one hit. Kept moving, its armour holds up better, and good mobility on any terrain suits flanking. It was the Battle Pass Season XIX "First Sample" reward.
ussr_t_50: Designed from 1939 by a team including L. Troyanov at Leningrad's Factory No. 185 to replace the T-26 and BT, the T-50 grew from the T-126 prototype; disruption from the Great Purge, manufacturing difficulty and a higher cost than the T-34 stopped production after 69 tanks. In the game it is effectively a small T-34, with well-sloped plating and a serviceable 45 mm gun, and is best used as a close-range brawler. That makes it a useful introduction to the Soviet style of play. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_t_54_1947: The first T-54, built from 1946 to 1948, had a 100 mm D-10T gun, the new V-54 engine and a streamlined turret with a wide mantlet; its trials went badly and production paused until the Model 1949 arrived, the start of a family still in service today. In the game it combines dependable armour, a good gun and fair mobility, though HEAT rounds are increasingly common, so cover still matters. The turret is strong but has a shot trap at the front. Played sensibly it is a powerful tank. It was added in Update 1.43.
ussr_t_54_1949: Built from 1949 to 1952, the second T-54 model gained an IS-3-inspired domed turret with flat sides and no frontal shot trap, wider tracks, a modernised transmission and conventional bow machine-gun mounts. In the game the new turret offers slightly better protection, offset by weaker hull armour, and it gains APDS, which penetrates very well but does little damage afterwards, so it is best kept for the toughest targets. It arrived in Update 1.47 "Big Guns".
ussr_t_54_1951: The Model 1951 T-54, made from 1952 to 1954, brought a hemispherical turret, the TSh-2-22 telescopic sight and an engine smoke system that sprays diesel into the exhaust to create a screen, a feature later used on the T-55 and T-62. In the game it plays almost exactly like the Model 1949 but adds a HEATFS round that penetrates 380 mm; its weak effect after penetration makes it a secondary option rather than the main load. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_t_55_am: Launched in the 1970s to keep the T-55 competitive, the T-55AM programme added passive appliqué armour, the Volna fire-control upgrade, optional Bastion guided projectiles and automotive improvements; the "-1" denotes the stronger V-46-5M engine, derived from the T-72's. In the game it balances strong armour, firepower and mobility well enough to rank among the best all-rounders at its level, a clear step up from the T-55A in every respect. It has been sold as a premium pack since Update 1.81 "The Valkyries".
ussr_t_55_amd_1: The T-55AMD-1 adds the Drozd hard-kill active protection system, developed in the late 1970s to shield T-55s and T-62s from ATGMs and hand-held rockets; around 250 T-55As were converted to carry it. In the game it shares the T-55AM-1's gun, fire control, engine and hull upgrades but swaps the "brow" turret armour for Drozd, which can intercept ATGMs across an 80° frontal arc, making it better against missile-armed IFVs, tank destroyers and helicopters. Without the brow armour the turret will not reliably stop tank rounds, but the 100 mm D-10T2S, with APFSDS, APHE and ATGMs, and adequate mobility keep it effective. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
ussr_t_55a: Produced from 1963 to 1981, the T-55A added anti-radiation lead lining, a full PAZ/FVU filtration system and room for six more 100 mm rounds where the hull machine gun had been, with a roof-mounted DShK fitted from 1970. In the game its armour is much like late T-54s, while a stronger engine lifts its top speed slightly despite the extra weight. APFSDS with 335 mm of penetration at point-blank and high velocity makes long-range shots easier, and a fully automatic two-plane stabiliser allows accurate fire on the move. It arrived in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
ussr_t_60_1941: Designed by Nicholas Astrov's team at Moscow Factory No. 37, the T-60 was a wartime stopgap built on the T-40's chassis, giving up its ability to swim for thicker armour; its 20 mm TNSh, derived from the ShVAK aircraft cannon, penetrated only 15 mm at 500 m, so it shifted to infantry support and later spawned the T-70. In the game a nimble chassis and sloped front armour suit almost any approach, but the weak gun rarely penetrates frontally, so flanking is the way to use it. Each small magazine is followed by a long reload. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_t_62: Developed from the T-55, whose low profile and thick turret it kept, the T-62 introduced the smoothbore gun to production tanks, firing high-velocity APFSDS; it became the Soviet Army's new spearhead but never fully displaced the cheaper, simpler T-55 in export sales. In the game it is the Soviet entry point to modern combat, with armour much like the T-55's and a gun and ammunition that can handle even well-protected opponents. The slow reload hurts when several enemies appear at once, so it does better hanging back from the front and playing patiently. It arrived in Update 1.61 "Road to Glory".
ussr_t_62m1: The T-62M-1 modernised the T-62 with BDD appliqué armour on the glacis and turret front, belly and side protection, an anti-neutron liner, Volna fire control with a KTD-2 laser rangefinder, a two-plane stabiliser, a ballistic computer, the Sheksna system for gun-launched 9M117 Bastion missiles and a V-46-5M diesel. BDD brings frontal protection close to the first T-64 and T-72 and defeats 84 and 90 mm rounds. In the game its very strong turret and varied ammunition suit hull-down sniping and support, while close fights expose its weaknesses. It arrived in Update 1.79 "Project X".
ussr_t_64_b_1984: The third T-64 model brought a revised armour layout, the 1A33 fire-control system, the 9K112-1 Kobra missile system, the upgraded 2A46-2 125 mm gun, a two-plane stabiliser and a new autoloader, with the glacis thickened from 1985. In the game its three-layer composite hull resists most hits and a wide ammunition selection deals with any target, while the low profile lets it use cover other tanks cannot, though the engine feels underpowered. An optional Kontakt-1 ERA kit reshapes the hull and turret with distinctive wedge-shaped blocks. It arrived in Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm".
ussr_t_64a_1971: Designed as Object 434 to boost the T-64's firepower, the T-64A received the powerful 125 mm D-81T; with only about 25 rounds able to fit and no room to enlarge the hull, designers replaced the loader with the first autoloader in a Soviet MBT, cutting the crew to three. In the game the gun hits hard, but protection is mediocre, mobility unremarkable and reversing painfully slow, so it works best as a careful, defensive sniper using terrain for cover. Many opponents can penetrate its hull and outmanoeuvre it, so watching the flanks is essential. It arrived in Update 1.71 "New E.R.A.".
ussr_t_70_1942: N. Astrov's T-70 upgraded the T-60 with a new turret and a 45 mm 20-K, served until 1948 and formed the basis of the SU-76 and ZSU-37; in 1944 Sergeant Alexander Pegov used one to ambush a column of about 18 German tanks, knocking out a Panther and earning the Hero of the Soviet Union title. In the game it can penetrate almost everything it meets, and being small and low it is well suited to ambushes and flanking. The armour is well sloped, but with only two crew any penetration is usually fatal. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_t_72a: The second T-72 model, part of a family of almost 25,000 tanks, swapped the original optical rangefinder for the TPD-K1 laser unit, added electronic fire control and heavily armoured the turret front with composite, with provision for ERA and smoke launchers; many early "Ural" tanks were later brought up to this standard. In the game the composite turret front shrugs off many shots and the gun is powerful and accurate. The engine copes well with rough ground, but acceleration, hull traverse and reverse speed lag behind Western rivals. It arrived in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
ussr_t_72av_turms: Syria modernised its export T-72M1s with Italian help, around the Galileo TURMS-T fire-control system: between 1998 and 2000, 124 tanks received second-generation thermal and stabilised sights for gunner and commander, an improved stabiliser and the ability to fire 9M119 Refleks missiles. In the game it has less armour than the T-72B and shares the family's slow gun elevation and a reverse of only 4 km/h, but thermal sights for both crewmen make finding targets far easier. Paired with the strong 3BM42 round it makes a very good long-range and support tank. It arrived as a premium pack in the "New Power" update.
ussr_t_72b: The third T-72 model brought the 125 mm 2A46M with a 2E42-2 two-plane stabiliser, the 1A40-1 fire-control system with a sight for firing 9M119 Svir missiles through the barrel, 20 mm of extra hull-front armour and an 840 hp V-84-1 engine. In the game its turret and hull are very well protected, but it is slower than Western rivals, has no thermal imaging and reverses slowly, which makes close-range fights dangerous. It suits support, flanking and sniping from a little way back, where the strong frontal armour counts most. It arrived in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
ussr_t_72b3_2011: From 2010 Russia began upgrading stored T-72Bs with T-90 components to simplify logistics, creating the T-72B3 (Object 184M-3). The programme centred on new fire control, including the Sosna-U panoramic sight with thermal imaging and a built-in laser rangefinder for the gunner, alongside engine, steering and track upgrades. In the game the gunner's thermal imager makes spotting enemies at range much easier, and the upgrades as a whole make it one of the strongest T-72s. The very slow reverse remains its main flaw. It arrived in the "Raining Fire" update.
ussr_t_72b3_arena: Arena, adopted in 1993, followed the Soviet Drozd, the first APS built in quantity, in detecting and intercepting incoming grenades and missiles; its export version, Arena-E, was shown on a T-72B3 at the 2013 Russia Arms Expo in Nizhny Tagil, though that tank was not a production model. In the game this event reward differs from the T-72B3A by carrying fewer countermeasures, no Relikt ERA on the sides and a weaker engine. It keeps a hard-hitting 125 mm and reasonable armour, but reverse speed and gun depression are poor. It was the reward for the "Paintball Arena" event.
ussr_t_72b3_arena_m: The T-72B3A adds the Arena-M active protection system, a development of the Soviet Arena that uses radar to spot incoming ATGMs and RPG grenades and fires counter-munitions to destroy them 5-10 m from the tank; KBM first showed it on a T-72 in 2013. In the game it keeps its predecessor's gun and armour but cannot fit the second layer of Relikt on the hull sides, relying instead on Arena-M for all-round defence against ground- and air-launched missiles. Most kinetic rounds get past the system, and the T-72's poor reverse remains. It arrived in the "Leviathans" update.
ussr_t_72b_1989: The 1989 T-72B adds Kontakt-5 explosive reactive armour, the first ERA anywhere able to significantly reduce APFSDS penetration, and extra composite armour on the turret sides. In the game the gun and structure match the regular T-72B, but the much better protection allows a somewhat more aggressive approach. The slow reverse still makes narrow streets risky, since backing out of trouble is hard. It arrived in the "Raining Fire" update.
ussr_t_72m2_moderna: After Czechoslovakia split, Slovakia's ZTS Dubnica teamed with Belgium's SABCA and France's SFIM to upgrade the T-72M1, adding an upgraded 2A46MS gun, French electro-optics with VEGA Plus fire control, modular armour, a 30 mm 2A42 autocannon and a new diesel. Shown at IDET 1994, it attracted no buyers, and a 1998 Slovak order for five ended with a single unfinished prototype. In the game it brings French thermal sights, new ERA and APFSDS and better mobility than most T-72s, and its BMP-2-style 30 mm cannon adds useful extra firepower. It was a "Battle for Arachis" event reward in the "Wind of Change" update.
ussr_t_80: Because the two-man T-70 overloaded its commander, who also aimed, loaded and worked the radio, the T-80 light tank gave it a larger turret for a third crewman with higher gun elevation, thicker hull sides and a stronger engine; only 120 were built before all Soviet light tank production stopped in October 1943. In the game the extra crewman shortens the reload and improves survivability, but the armour means little against the opponents it meets, and a hit through the centre can still kill the whole crew. The turret traverses at just 4.2° per second. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_t_80b: Born from efforts to put a gas turbine into a T-64A-derived tank, the Object 219 beat the T-72 and T-64A on mobility in trials and, despite high fuel use and early unreliability, became the T-80; the T-80B entered production in 1976 with T-64B-derived ATGM fire control and "K" ceramic armour. In the game it looks much like the T-64B, sharing the rounded turret, skirts and 125 mm gun, but adds a 30 mm plate on the glacis and a snorkel, and its NSVT has 150-round boxes. The key difference is the far stronger engine, which gives much better mobility. It arrived in Update 1.81 "The Valkyries".
ussr_t_80bvm: The T-80BVM is Omsktransmash's late-2010s upgrade of the T-80BV, with Relikt ERA arranged like the T-72B3's, side ERA packages, a gun system for the newest Russian ammunition, all-electric gun drives, new thermal sights and the T-80U's 1,250 hp GTD-1250 turbine; since 2018 it has been the standard for the remaining T-80BV fleet. In the game third-generation Relikt protects well against both HEAT and kinetic rounds, the gun fires 3BM60 "Svinets" APFSDS and Refleks missiles, and the engine gives strong mobility. Combined with a low profile, it is a fitting top of the T-64/T-80 line. It arrived in the "Red Skies" update.
ussr_t_80u: Among the most capable tanks the Soviet Union fielded, the T-80U thoroughly reworked the T-80B with a new turret, Kontakt-5 ERA, about 14% more engine power, 3BM46 APFSDS and 9M119 missiles. In the game its armour resists both chemical and kinetic rounds well, its power-to-weight ratio matches the Leopard 2A4 and IPM1, and its low profile and strong gun make it very versatile. Crew survival after a penetration is weak and reverse speed modest, though better than on the T-64 and T-72. It arrived in Update 1.87 "Locked On".
ussr_t_80u_yt_cup_2019: Adopted in 1985 to fix the original T-80's armour and turbine shortcomings, the T-80U added Kontakt-5 ERA, a new gun and improved fire control, though production with the GTD-1250 engine only began in 1990; it serves in Ukraine, Russia, Cyprus and South Korea. This version, with unique camouflage, was awarded to YouTube Cup 2019 winners. Its mobility, firepower and very strong armour let it match even more modern tanks, its main weaknesses being the usual cramped Soviet interior and shallow gun depression.
ussr_t_80ud: The T-80UD "Bereza" ("Birch") of 1985 replaced the fuel-hungry turbine of the T-80U with a 1,000 hp 6TD opposed-piston diesel originally meant for the T-64, and after 1991 it became the basis for Ukraine's T-84 family. In the game it amounts to a de-rated T-80U: power-to-weight falls from 27 to about 22 hp/ton, below the T-80B but above the T-72B, and it lacks thermal sights and the best 3BM46 APFSDS. In every other respect it remains a T-80U, so against the opponents a T-72B meets it is competitive thanks to tough armour, a quick reload and respectable mobility. It arrived in the "Alpha Strike" update.
ussr_t_80ue1: With T-80UD diesels hard to service in Russia and the T-80BV outdated, Russia mounted turrets from retired T-80UDs on T-80BV hulls, adding a second-generation thermal imager, an autoloader that takes longer APFSDS, hull Kontakt-5 and a stronger engine; the T-80UE-1 entered service in 2005, with no more than a hundred built. In the game its ammunition ranges from capable APFSDS and tandem ATGMs to large HE-frag shells, and the autoloader, slightly slower than NATO loaders, is unaffected by crew losses. The thermal sight and quicker turret set it apart from other Soviet tanks, though survivability and reverse speed are poor. It arrived in Update 2.37 "Seek & Destroy".
ussr_t_80ue1_sm: This T-80UE-1 from the 2025 Senrai Maidens event carries a unique exterior themed on the character Maria and otherwise matches the other premium T-80UE-1. The type itself combined T-80UD turrets with T-80BV hulls, a second-generation thermal imager and hull Kontakt-5, entering Russian service in 2005. In the game its varied ammunition, from APFSDS and tandem ATGMs to powerful HE-frag, an autoloader unaffected by crew losses, a good thermal sight and quick turret traverse make it a strong all-rounder, though a dense interior and slow reverse leave it fragile.
ussr_t_80uk: The T-80UK was a 1980s command-tank prototype of the T-80U with a thermal sight, Shtora-1 soft-kill protection, new fire control and extra communications; it was certified in the 1990s, yet service examples lacked Shtora-1, probably for budget reasons, and the sole prototype now appears at exhibitions. In the game it plays like its tech-tree predecessor, adding Shtora sensors and IR jammers and an HE-TF version of the 3OF26 shell. Its APFSDS is not the best at its level, struggling against strong upper plates such as the ZTZ99's, and Soviet gun handling is sluggish, so every shot matters. It was added as a squadron vehicle in the "Drone Age" update.
ussr_t_80um2: The T-80UM2 (Object 219AS-M) was a late-1990s Omsktransmash prototype testing a T-80U upgrade with the Drozd hard-kill active protection system; Russia's economic troubles halted work, and it was only shown at a 1997 demonstration. In the game it performs like the T-80U but adds Drozd to shoot down incoming missiles, improving survivability and making it an easy tank to pick up. Its fire control lacks a thermal channel, though. It was the 2022 Winter Quest reward in the "Apex Predators" update.
ussr_t_90a: Intended to succeed the T-72 as the Soviet spearhead, the T-90A brought a 125 mm 2A46, a gunner's thermal sight, 1A45T fire control and a more powerful engine, with Kontakt-5 ERA and the Shtora-1 system, which warns of laser designation and jams SACLOS missile guidance once the turret faces the threat. In the game it plays like other Soviet MBTs, with a low silhouette and tough front that suit support, flanking and sniping. The slow reverse makes close fighting a last resort, so taking a hull-down spot early and covering the push works best. It arrived in the "New Power" update.
ussr_t_90m_2020: The T-90M (Object 188M), nicknamed "Proryv-3" ("Breakthrough-3"), is Russia's latest mass-produced MBT, first seen in 2017 with a new welded turret, a remote weapon station, improved fire control, a new engine and a revised autoloader and ammunition layout for better survivability. In the game it adds Relikt ERA, a better powerplant and an upgraded turret and fire control, bringing it up to modern standards of protection, although the long-standing Soviet weakness in reverse speed remains. It arrived in the "Air Superiority" update.
ussr_t_90m_arena_m: This version of the T-90M carries the Arena-M active protection system, with modules fitted inside the tank's outline; it was patented in April 2023, first shown in February 2025 and put into production after trials in June 2026. In the game it matches the standard T-90M apart from the APS: excellent frontal and side armour handle chemical and kinetic rounds, and advanced fire control lets it engage ground and air targets with APFSDS and airburst HE. Mobility trails most rivals because of limited power for its weight and a slow reverse, and penetrations tend to hit vital modules and crew despite spall liners. It arrived in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
ussr_to_55: The TO-55 was a T-55 with an ATO-200 flamethrower mounted coaxially, fed from a 460-litre tank in place of the bow ammunition rack and reaching about 200 m, giving infantry a better-protected flame weapon against fortified positions. In the game it is essentially a T-55A carrying T-54 (1951) ammunition, so compared with the T-54 it gains the D-10T2S, a two-plane stabiliser, engine smoke, the 3D3 smoke shell, night vision and a stronger engine. It carries fewer rounds than the T-54, with 25 and a smaller ready rack, and the flamethrower is short-ranged and only useful against open or light vehicles. It arrived in the "Sons of Attila" update.
ussr_tor_m1: The 9K330 Tor short-range missile system entered Soviet service in 1986 after more than a decade of work, and NPO Antey immediately began improving it; the 9K331 Tor-M1, with a second target channel, a stronger warhead and better low-altitude engagement, cleared trials in 1989 and entered Russian service in 1991. In the game its biggest asset is the ability to engage two targets at once. Its armament is limited to vertically launched missiles, however, so it has no way to fight armoured vehicles up close. It arrived in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
ussr_type_62: China's Type 62, developed by China North Industries Corporation from the Type 59 with a smaller gun, lighter armour and reduced equipment, entered service in 1963 for reconnaissance and support in the rugged south of the country; about 1,500 were built by 1989. The Soviet tree's example, a reward from the 2016 "Winter Holiday" event, carries the 85 mm Type 63 gun with a broad ammunition choice that works at any range. Its low profile and agility suit maps with thick vegetation and rough terrain, where it can reach unexpected spots and set up ambushes.
ussr_type_65_aa: Probably improvised by North Vietnam in the mid-1960s, this anti-aircraft conversion put an open-topped box turret with twin Chinese 37 mm Type 65 cannons on a T-34-85 hull; everything known comes from one example captured by US forces and displayed at Fort Sill, Oklahoma, and the name was created for the game. It was a reward from the 2017 "Operation S.U.M.M.E.R." event. The turret only stops rifle-calibre fire, it stands taller than a T-34-85 and nearby blasts can knock it out, but fast turret traverse, a decent firing rate and HVAP ammunition make it useful for both air defence and flanking.
ussr_valentine_mk_9: Added for Valentine's Day in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind", this gift tank is a British Valentine IX of the kind shipped to the Soviet Union under Lend-Lease. It has since come back for Golden Eagles during the Valentine's Day mini-events held each year from 2020 to 2023, rather than through the tech tree.
ussr_zis_12_94KM_1945: The ZiS-12 was a long-wheelbase version of the ZiS-5 truck built at Moscow's ZiS plant, and in wartime some carried twin 25 mm 72-K autocannons to protect ground troops from air attack. In the game it fills the same role as the GAZ-MM (72-K): rapid fire for engaging aircraft, plus armour-piercing belts for lightly armoured vehicles. It carries plenty of ammunition, but sustained bursts empty it quickly, so trigger discipline matters. It arrived in Update 1.57 "Battle March".
ussr_zis_30: Two weeks into the 1941 German invasion, V.G. Grabin produced the ZiS-30 by putting the 57 mm ZiS-2 anti-tank gun on a T-20 Komsomolets artillery tractor; simple to build, mobile and with a wide firing arc, it was accepted at once, and around 100 were made. In the game the gun is exceptionally strong for its rank, often killing in one shot and handling higher-ranked tanks too. Protection is practically absent, so it relies on speed and a small, if tall, profile for sniping or hit-and-run attacks, and the recoil briefly pins it after each shot. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_zis_43: Built in 1942 as a prototype, the ZiS-43 was a half-track carrying a 37 mm 61-K autocannon behind thin plates for the crew, and it never went past the trial stage. In the game it takes a lot of practice: the gun is potent and can penetrate most ground targets from the side, but the vehicle is tall, slow, unstable and poorly armoured, too sluggish to flank effectively. Against aircraft the modest rate of fire demands precise lead and well-placed hits. It arrived in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
ussr_zprk_2s6: The 2S6 (2K22, NATO "SA-19 Grison") replaced the ZSU-23-4, which could no longer cope with late Cold War aircraft and helicopters; work began around 1970 but slowed until Arab-Israeli War experience showed guns react faster than missile-only systems, and it entered service in 1984. In the game it pairs two twin-barrelled 30 mm autocannons, effective against aircraft and against ground vehicles showing their sides, with eight 9M311 missiles for distant or high targets. Its large size and a fixed, high-magnification optical channel take some getting used to. It arrived in Update 1.87 "Locked On".
ussr_zsu_23_4: Fielded from 1965 on an ASU-85-derived hull, the ZSU-23-4 Shilka brought radar fire control, a stabiliser for firing on the move and a search radar, replaced the ZSU-57-2 by the 1970s and saw combat worldwide, including in Afghanistan, where radar-less versions with extra ammunition were used against ground targets. In the game its four guns let it fill the sky with shells, making it extremely effective against aircraft within about 2 km. Compared with the ZSU-37-2 Yenisei before it in the tree, it lacks range and the penetration to reliably defeat tank sides. It arrived in Update 1.63 "Desert Hunters".
ussr_zsu_23_4m2: In Afghanistan, the BTR-70 and BMP-1 could not elevate their weapons enough for mountain fighting while the ZSU-23-4 could rake high slopes, so about 18 Shilkas had their radar removed and the space filled with extra ammunition, with a few more converted in 1999. In the game the four fast-firing guns still deal well with jets even without radar, and the doubled ammunition load allows long bursts. Against ground targets it can only penetrate unarmoured or very light vehicles, and heavy machine-gun fire defeats its armour, so aircraft gunners and artillery are a serious threat. It arrived in Update 2.39 "Dance of Dragons".
ussr_zsu_23_4m4: The 1999 M4 modernisation, probably driven by tight 1990s budgets, gave Russia's ageing Shilkas a digital fire-control computer in place of the analogue one, a datalink to the PPRU-1 command vehicle, refreshed mechanical systems and pairs of 9K38 Igla missiles. In the game it still suffers from the Shilka's weak radar, but the Igla missiles are accurate and reach further than the quad 23 mm guns, extending its useful range considerably. It arrived in the "Alpha Strike" update.
ussr_zsu_29k: The 29-K was a 1930s Soviet anti-aircraft conversion of the YaG-10 truck, carrying a 76 mm M1931 AA gun on a strengthened bed as a cheaper alternative to the cancelled T-28-based SU-8; 40 to 61 were built and used against both aircraft and tanks early in the war. In the game, like the German 8,8 cm Flak 37 Sfl., it serves as a tank destroyer: the gun reloads quickly, fires fast shells and penetrates well. With no protection beyond its six crew and only average mobility, it should be used purely as a sniper, firing from behind cover with just the rear exposed. It arrived in Update 1.67 "Assault".
ussr_zsu_37: Developed in 1943 after costly losses among air-defence vehicles, the ZSU-37 put a 37 mm 61-K cannon on the SU-76M chassis; trials ended in February 1944, production began in 1945, and about 375 were built by 1948, though its combat record is unknown. In the game the gun's rate of fire is middling, but a few hits readily sever a wing or tail, and AP rounds go through most tanks' side armour. The compact, open-topped layout leaves it very vulnerable to air attack and artillery. It was added in Update 1.43.
ussr_zsu_37_2: Begun in 1957 because the ZSU-57-2 lacked accuracy and radar, the ZSU-37-2 Yenisei used a modified SU-100P chassis and was developed alongside the Shilka but tasked with protecting tank units against aircraft up to 3,000 m; trials went well, yet in 1962 only the Shilka was accepted. In the game it out-ranges the Shilka and penetrates ground targets better, though it fires more slowly, and it is faster, more agile and lower. The radar is weak, though: its narrow 15° vertical scan struggles with high-flying targets and lock-ons need precise aim. It arrived in the "Hot Tracks" update.
ussr_zsu_57_2: Designed at NII-58 between 1947 and 1950, the ZSU-57-2 married Grabin's twin 57 mm S-68 anti-aircraft gun to a lightened T-54 chassis to give it mobility; 857 were built from 1955 to 1960 and saw combat from Vietnam and the Six-Day War to Iraq and Yugoslavia. In the game its slow-firing guns struggle against fast early jets and are only somewhat better against helicopters. Where it shines is as an improvised tank hunter: good ballistics, decent mobility and strong AP shells let it fight light vehicles and even some medium tanks and early MBTs head-on. It was added in Update 1.43.
ussr_zut_37: In 1942 B.G. Shpitalny proposed mounting his 37 mm Sh-37 gun in a new T-70 turret, and OKB-15 built the ZUT-37 that August, but trials revealed a five-minute reload for the 20-round magazine, an unreliable, inaccurate gun and a 25-second half-turn of the turret; a revised version in 1943 failed to revive interest, and the project ended. In the game it is nearly useless against aircraft for similar reasons, but the automatic 37 mm on the T-70 chassis turns it into a capable light tank, able to take on several enemies in a row and helped by its small size and speed. It was added in Update 1.43.
v_11g: Vultee's V-1 airliner was halted at 25 airframes by new regulations, but its attack derivatives found buyers: China's Nationalist air force bought 30 V-11s, planning to assemble them locally, and flew them with mercenary pilots against Japanese-held targets early in the war before retiring them by 1940. In the game it is large for its rank and lightly armed, but its fairly tight turn can surprise careless opponents, occasionally even biplanes. Its bombs can still destroy ground targets, making it a reasonable introduction to attack aircraft. It arrived in the "Hot Tracks" update.
v_12d: The V-12D was a later Vultee attack derivative that China's Nationalist government ordered after the V-11, with a stronger engine and somewhat better armament; because of the blockade, only three or four reached China as kits after the move to Yunnan, and there is no record of any being assembled or flying in combat. In the game it carries the same weak ground payload as the V-11, but its uprated engine and two nose-mounted .50 cal guns make it the better of the pair, and it can even act as a stopgap fighter against early fighters that ignore their tails. It arrived in the "Ground Breaking" update.
v_156_b1: The Chesapeake was the British name for the V-156-B1, an export SB2U Vindicator originally ordered by France; after France fell, the Fleet Air Arm took over the order with an extra fuel tank, more armour and four forward-firing Brownings. Meant for anti-submarine work from HMS Archer, it proved underpowered with too small a load and ended up as a trainer. In the game it is slow because of its weak engine, but four forward guns plus a rear gunner let it fight most opponents it meets, and its bomb load handles ground targets, though dive-bombing vehicles takes practice in realistic battles. It arrived in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
v_156_f: France bought the SB2U-2 as the V-156-F in 1939, fitting French radios and 7.5 mm guns plus the dive brakes the US Navy had rejected; meant for the carrier Béarn, its squadrons moved ashore when the ship was judged too slow, and flew until the armistice. In the game it is slow but sturdy and built for diving onto targets, and its wing-mounted air brakes, rare on early aircraft, help keep the wings intact in steep dives. Its payload is small, at up to 200 kg, though wing guns can strafe soft targets, and the rear gunner offers only modest protection. It arrived in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
vampire_fb5: De Havilland's Vampire began in 1941 around the company's Halford H.1 (later Goblin) turbojet, with twin tail booms allowing a short jet pipe; it first flew in September 1943, and the FB.5 of 1948, the most numerous version with over 1,000 built, added engine armour, shortened wings and underwing points for bombs and rockets. In the game it is slow for a jet but very agile, rather like a jet-powered Spitfire: it cannot outrun rivals, but it can draw them into turning fights and win with four Hispano cannons on a steady platform. Keeping energy up after committing to a turn is crucial. It arrived in Update 1.33.
vampire_fb52_finland: Finland bought six FB 52A Vampires from Britain in 1953, nicknamed "Vamppi", followed by nine T.55 trainers in 1955; they were operated by the 1st and 2nd Air Wings until 1965. In the game it behaves like a typical early jet, with weak acceleration and a lower top speed than its rivals, traded for strong dogfighting performance. It turns very tightly while it has speed, but bleeds energy easily, so precise shooting and short engagements serve it best. It arrived in the "Fire and Ice" update.
