vampire_fb52a_italy: After earlier F.3 and FB.5 models, Italy bought 51 FB.52A Vampires, whose Goblin 3 out-powered the FB.5's Goblin 2, then built 195 more locally at FIAT and Macchi before replacing them with F-84G Thunderjets in 1960. In the game it is a capable turn fighter thanks to strong low-speed handling, which gives it an edge over most enemy jets, though it accelerates poorly despite the stronger engine. Four Hispano Mk.V cannons hit hard, and in ground battles its light ordnance can knock out armoured vehicles. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
vampire_fb5_j28b: Sweden bought the Vampire FB 5 as the J 28B from 1949, and once the last arrived in 1952 its air force had no piston fighters left; replaced as fighters by the J 29 and J 34 in 1956, they were reassigned to attack work as the A 28B. In the game it shares the Vampire family's excellent dogfighting, so a skilled pilot can hold off several opponents. That agility comes at the expense of thrust, however, and its weak acceleration lets fast piston fighters catch it once it has bled speed in a fight. It arrived in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
vb_10_02: The Arsenal VB.10 began in 1937 as a single-engine interceptor, was frozen by the 1940 invasion and was reworked after liberation with a second engine behind the pilot driving contra-rotating propellers. The second prototype, the VB.10-02, flew in September 1946 with six .50 cal Brownings added to four Hispano cannons, but cooling problems led to its loss in an in-flight fire in January 1948, and the project was cancelled that September. In the game it has devastating firepower but flies essentially like the VB.10C-1 despite facing tougher opposition, so it should pick fights carefully rather than dogfight dedicated fighters. It arrived in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
vb_10c1: Derived from the V.G.33, the VB.10C-1 was a French heavy fighter; 200 were ordered in 1946, cut to 50 and finally cancelled, France relying on American F6F, F8F and F4U types until its own jets were ready. In the game its two Hispano-Suiza 12Z engines, one hidden behind the pilot and driving its own propeller set, make it look like a single-engined super-prop. It is fast but heavy and poor in a dogfight, so with four 20 mm cannons and a high top speed it is best flown boom-and-zoom after climbing away from the fight early in the match.
venom_fb4: Planned as the Vampire FB.8, the de Havilland Venom became a new design to an Air Ministry requirement for an interim fighter-bomber, keeping the Vampire's look but adding the far more powerful Ghost engine; it first flew in September 1949 and entered service in 1952, the FB.4 being the RAF's final variant with ejection seats and powered ailerons. In the game it keeps the Vampire's agility with much more thrust, letting it compete in both energy and turning fights. Against later opponents, some with afterburners, it falls back on Vampire tactics: holding speed and luring lone enemies into turns. It arrived in Update 1.43.
vg_33: Arsenal's V.G.33C-1 grew from Michel Vernisse and Jean Galtier's V.G.30 of 1936 and first flew in April 1939 with a Hispano-Suiza 12Y-31 engine; orders reached 1,000, but only 19 had been delivered by the 1940 armistice and it never saw combat. In the game it is quick, agile and hard-hitting, climbs superbly and performs well at altitude. Against that, it carries little 20 mm ammunition, the airframe is fragile and it rolls sluggishly. It arrived in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
vl_myrsky_2_late: The Myrsky ("Storm") was Finland's home-grown fighter, chosen in 1939 but only developed in earnest from 1940 after Finland was cut off from Allied suppliers; refining the airframe and engine dragged on until 1943, and it reached combat units in August 1944, too late to make a significant difference. In the game it does not fly exceptionally well, but strong machine guns and a good turn of speed for an early monoplane give it real fighting ability. It was a reward from the 2021 "Summer Landing" event.
walrus_mk1: Supermarine developed the Seagull V as a catapult-launched spotter for the Royal Australian Air Force, which ordered 24 after 1933 trials; the Royal Navy then ordered a modified version as the Walrus Mk.I, and 740 were built by 1944 for scouting, rescue and submarine hunting, some serving abroad until 1958. In the game it is unusually well armed for a ship-based seaplane, with 7.7 mm guns in front and rear turrets and four 250 lb bombs that let it act as a light bomber, and wheels let it use airfields and carriers. Mediocre flight performance and poor manoeuvrability are its main limits. It arrived in Update 2.13 "Winged Lions".
washington_b1: Needing a modern bomber in the early 1950s while its Lincolns aged and jet bombers were still in development, the RAF borrowed 87 B-29 Superfortresses from the USAF as the Washington B.1; the Canberra replaced them from 1953, and the last were retired in 1958 and returned to the US. In the game it is identical to the American B-29: a pure heavy bomber built to carry a huge load a long way. Since it often meets early jets, high altitude is its best protection, with many .50 cal guns to deter interceptors that do get close. It arrived in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
wasp_has_mk1: Westland's Wasp was a small shipborne helicopter from the MATCH programme, designed to carry two homing torpedoes and later SS.11 wire-guided missiles, with no guns since they were not needed for anti-submarine work; the first pre-production example flew in October 1962. In the game it follows the Scout in the British tree with a similar but harder style: no armour, no countermeasures, less mobility and no fixed armament. For pilots who persevere, its small profile, good agility and the Scout's hard-hitting missile payload make it dangerous. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
welkin_fmk1: Spurred by high-flying German Ju 86P bombers, Westland adapted its Whirlwind into the Welkin high-altitude interceptor, with a much larger wing, Merlin engines and a pressurised cabin; it first flew in November 1942, but the thick wing made it prone to stalls, it was heavy, and by its May 1944 service debut high-altitude Spitfires already did the job, so only 77 were built and none saw combat. In the game it has powerful guns, good vertical performance and solid high-altitude handling, but it is slow in level flight and rolls sluggishly. It arrived in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
wellington_mk10: Built in greater numbers than any other Wellington, the Mk X resembled the Mk III but had Bristol Hercules XVIII engines that cost a little top speed, and it formed the basis of many Coastal Command anti-submarine and anti-shipping versions. In the game it is agile for a bomber and carries a flexible load, from two Mk XII torpedoes for ships to the huge 4,000 lb HC Mk II bomb for ground targets. Bombs and defensive guns match the Mk III, but it is slightly slower and cannot escape contemporary fighters, so escorts make a big difference. It has been in the game since the open beta before Update 1.27.
wellington_mk1c: Named, like the Vickers Wellesley, after the Duke of Wellington, the Wellington was designed to a 1932 Air Ministry specification with Barnes Wallis's light but sturdy geodetic structure; the Mk Ic replaced the troublesome Vickers turrets of the Mk I with Frazer-Nash units, swapped the ventral turret for two beam guns and revised the hydraulics and electrics. In the game it handles well for a bomber and can carry torpedoes or a 4,000 lb HC bomb, but its six 7.7 mm guns give weak defence and it cannot outrun fighters, so friendly cover is important. It has been in the game since the open beta before Update 1.27.
wellington_mk1c_late: Combat experience led Vickers to move the Mk Ic's side gun positions further aft and plate over the windows, with aircraft already built modified in the field; 2,685 Mk Ics were produced and flew in the early war years. In the game it is practically the same as the earlier Mk Ic: tough enough to absorb plenty of machine-gun hits, with a good bomb load or torpedoes. It is slow, though, and its exposed, unarmoured 7.7 mm guns provide little defence. It has been in the game since the open beta before Update 1.27.
wellington_mk1c_luftwaffe: This German-flagged Wellington Mk Ic is a captured British bomber, sold as a Golden Eagle premium since the open beta before Update 1.27 and identical to the British version. Its versatility makes it a worthwhile substitute for the He 111 H-6, and its turrets have wide arcs on a stable platform, though their 7.7 mm guns rarely bring down attackers. If the flight controls are shot away, adjusting engine power can keep it flying steadily enough to keep fighting.
wellington_mk3: Following the Merlin-powered Mk II, the Wellington Mk III switched to Bristol Hercules III or XI engines and doubled the tail turret to four guns; it was built from late 1941 to late 1942 and later cleared for glider towing. In the game it is nimble for a bomber with the same choice of torpedoes or a 4,000 lb HC bomb, and is faster and better defended than the Mk Ic. Even so, it cannot outrun fighters of its time and benefits greatly from an escort. It has been in the game since the open beta before Update 1.27.
wessex_mk5: Westland developed the Wessex from Sikorsky's H-34, first flying it in 1958 with a Gazelle turboshaft; the HU Mk.5, of which about 100 were built, used twin Rolls-Royce Gnome engines for commando, amphibious and rescue work, fought in conflicts including Cyprus, Malaysia and the Falklands, and served Britain into the 1990s. In the game it resembles the H-34, but the twin Gnomes give far more power and better flight performance. It also gains 7.62 mm machine guns and can carry guided AS.11s and AS.12s alongside unguided rockets. Like the H-34, it has no armour. It arrived in the "Alpha Strike" update.
whirlwind_mk1: Westland's answer to a 1935 requirement for a four-cannon heavy fighter, the Whirlwind first flew in October 1938 with two Peregrine engines and four 20 mm Hispanos; 200 were ordered, but production stopped at 112 when Rolls-Royce ended Peregrine output to focus on the Merlin, and the Typhoon replaced it at the start of 1944. In the game it is a hard-hitting heavy fighter that handles well, but its top speed is low, agility falls away above 500 km/h, and each cannon carries only 60 rounds. It arrived in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
whirlwind_p9: The Whirlwind P.9 represents the experimental pre-production stage of Westland's twin-engined fighter, the direct forerunner of the Whirlwind Mk I, whose development began in 1937. It is a gift aircraft, first handed out during the 2018 World War Two Chronicles in Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm" and returned in Update 1.91 "Night Vision" as the prize of the 2019 Operation "Shipyard" event.
wirraway: Australia's Commonwealth Aircraft Corporation built the CA-1 Wirraway from the American NA-16 design, starting in March 1939; used as light bombers in New Guinea and New Britain during 1942, Wirraways later returned to training and flew with the RAAF until 1959. In the game this premium is slow but very manoeuvrable and easy to fly, a good choice for beginners. Two fast-firing machine guns suit strafing light targets, while two 500 lb and two 250 lb bombs can destroy tougher ones. There is no bombsight in realistic battles, though, and the pilot is poorly protected. It has been in the game since the open beta before Update 1.27.
wm_21: Barred from having an air force by the Treaty of Trianon, Hungary licence-built the Fokker C.V before developing its own WM-16 and then the WM-21 Sólyom, with a stronger structure and new wings, which first flew in 1937; 128 were built and used for reconnaissance, the 1941 invasion of Yugoslavia and anti-partisan work until 1945. In the game it is slow and unwieldy, playing much like the Po-2, but it has reasonable guns and twelve 10 kg bombs. It arrived in the Italian tree in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
wm_23: With only three of 36 ordered He 112s delivered, Hungary designed its own fighter, the WM-23 Ezüst Nyíl, whose prototype flew in 1941 with a WM K-14B engine and impressed the military; the sole prototype crashed in April 1942, and with the Héja in service and Bf 109 licence production coming, the project was dropped. In the game it is very agile with excellent low-speed handling and decent guns, but it rolls poorly, has a low top speed and stiffens up at high speed. It arrived in the Italian tree in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
wyvern_s4: Conceived around the Rolls-Royce Eagle as a long-range strike aircraft for the Navy, the Wyvern was delayed when that engine was cancelled and eventually adopted the Armstrong Siddeley Python turboprop; it entered service in 1953 as the TF 4, later the S.4, and left the Fleet Air Arm in 1958. In the game its turboprop speed and broad choice of heavy ordnance make it a strong pick for combined battles. It can also fight aircraft, but engine power falls away above 3,000 m and it turns poorly, so boom-and-zoom attacks suit it far better than dogfights. It arrived in Update 1.59 "Flaming Arrows".
xa_38: Beech built two XA-38 "Grizzly" prototypes from 1942 as a possible A-20 replacement, first as a bomber hunter and then as a ground-attack aircraft with a 75 mm cannon in the nose and two twin .50 cal turrets; it tested well, but the B-29 programme claimed its R-3350 engines. In the game the 75 mm gun penetrates up to 104 mm, enough to defeat many vehicles from the side or through the engine deck, and with its bombs it is very dangerous in ground battles. Despite its turrets it is easy prey for fighters, especially once the gunner is hit. It arrived as a premium in Update 1.71 "New E.R.A.".
xf5f: Grumman's XF5F Skyrocket was a twin-engine carrier interceptor prototype for a 1938 Navy requirement, its stubby fuselage ending short of the wing's leading edge; it first flew on 1 April 1940 with two Wright R-1820s, its planned Madsen cannons replaced by machine guns, and it fed into the F7F Tigercat and XP-50 before a 1944 belly landing ended its career. In the game it is manoeuvrable and agile with a reasonable top speed and an armoured cockpit, though the engines are vulnerable. A pair each of heavy and light machine guns gives decent firepower. It was handed out in the 2013 "Winter Magic" event, arriving in Update 1.37.
xf5u_1: The Vought XF5U "Flying Pancake" used Charles Zimmermann's disc-like low-aspect-ratio wing, with two Twin Wasps driving wingtip propellers, to pair high speed with short take-offs; severe vibration kept the single finished prototype from flying, and after cancellation in 1947 it proved so tough it was demolished with a wrecking ball. In the game its stall speed is so low it can hang in a near-vertical climb, and with the wing doubling as fuselage it soaks up enormous damage. Otherwise it flies averagely, though it dives fast, but energy drains quickly in vertical manoeuvres and losing a propeller can mean an unrecoverable spin. It was the 2025 "Dreams Come True" reward.
xp-50: Grumman's XP-50 grew from a 1939 Army fighter competition: its Design 41, based on the XF5F, was kept as a backup to Lockheed's winning entry and became the XP-50 with turbocharged 1,200 hp R-1820s, but a turbocharger explosion destroyed the prototype and ended the project. In the game it climbs well above most opponents and is fairly agile, but it suffers from compression at speed and has no airbrakes, so dives need care. Two 20 mm cannons with limited ammunition and two 12.7 mm guns in the nose make it a good teacher of energy fighting and ammunition discipline. It has been a premium since Update 1.31.
xp-55: Curtiss-Wright's XP-55 Ascender came from a US push for radical fighter designs, using a lift-producing canard foreplane that allowed a smaller, lower-drag main wing; three prototypes were built, but performance gains over conventional fighters were too small and jets took priority. In the game it is unlike anything else in the American tree and demands energy tactics: it climbs and dives superbly, has reasonable agility and works best in boom-and-zoom attacks. All four guns are grouped in the nose for concentrated firepower. It arrived in Update 1.31.
yah_64: After the AH-56 Cheyenne was cancelled in 1972, the US Army's Advanced Attack Helicopter programme sought a faster, twin-engined, better-armed successor to the AH-1; Hughes' YAH-64 first flew in September 1975 and beat Bell's YAH-63 in 1976 thanks to its tougher four-blade rotor and steadier landing gear. In the game a thermal imager and AGM-114B Hellfires let it spot and hit targets up to 8 km away, beyond most SPAA apart from some radar SAMs, and a ballistic computer helps with Hydra-70 rockets. As an early Apache prototype it has no flares, chaff, IR countermeasures or air-to-air missiles. It arrived in the "Direct Hit" update.
yak-15: One of the Soviet Union's first jet fighters, the Yak-15 saved development time by fitting a reverse-engineered Jumo 004 to the Yak-3 airframe, and its familiar handling made it the type used to convert piston pilots to jets; 280 were built up to 1947. In the game the weak early jet engine, with 850 kgf stock, and a mere 60 rounds per gun make it demanding, especially against powerful late piston fighters. Its Yak-3 airframe keeps it extremely agile, and it loses less energy in turns than propeller aircraft, but regaining speed is slow, so climbing and keeping altitude in reserve is essential. It arrived in Update 1.31.
yak-15_early: The 15 aircraft now called the Yak-15P were a rushed batch for the November 1946 October Revolution parade, built when full-standard Yak-15s were running late; they lacked armour, many instruments and even guns, some carrying extra fuel instead, and the "P" designation was applied unofficially much later. In the game it keeps the Yak-3's superb handling and outturns most jets it meets, but low top speed, severe compression and weak acceleration leave it no escape when outnumbered. Carrying one 23 mm cannon fewer than the production Yak-15, it meets weaker opposition and can also provide air cover in combined battles. It arrived in Update 1.31.
yak-17: The Yak-17 refined the Yak-15, keeping the Yak-3 airframe but adding a bulletproof windscreen, extra fuel and modern tricycle landing gear like the MiG-9's; 430 were built, many going to Czechoslovakia and Poland, and it served as the main jet trainer for former piston pilots. In the game it is easy to underestimate: it holds speed in a straight line better than propeller fighters and turns well, so it can defend itself against props and jets alike. Low top speed and weak acceleration mean it should beat piston opponents on energy and avoid drawn-out duels with jets like the F-80C and F2H Banshee. It arrived in Update 1.33.
yak-1_early: Yakovlev's Yak-1 answered a 1938 call for a mainly wooden fighter that would be easy to build and repair; first flying in March 1939 as the Ya-26, it began a family that, across all Yak types, reached around 37,000 aircraft. In the game it is a good turn-fighter with strong energy retention, a fast dive and, for its rank, solid firepower from a 20 mm ShVAK and two ShKAS. It is at its best at low to medium altitude, as climb and performance fall off higher up, and its thin protection means head-on fire can kill the pilot or wreck the radiator. It arrived in Update 1.43.
yak-1b: The Yak-1B of autumn 1942 brought a stronger M-105P engine and a 12.7 mm Berezin UB in place of two ShKAS, along with electro-pneumatic firing, a Bf 109-style control stick, a new sight, a retractable tailwheel and better cooling; 4,188 were built, and all later Yak-1s followed this standard. In the game it performs well down low but poorly at altitude, and its airframe is much sturdier than the earlier Yak-1's. Firepower rises but ammunition is scarce, so short bursts are essential, and with no WEP it must avoid wasting energy. It has been in the game since the open beta before Update 1.27.
yak-1b_luftwaffe: In April 1943 a navigator's error led a squadron of 3rd Fighter Air Wing Yak-1Bs to the German-held airfield at Taganrog instead of Rostov; the first three to land came under fire and were captured, and the Germans later used the Yaks for deception, reconnaissance and surprise attacks. In the game this German example is an average low-altitude all-rounder, and its lack of glaring flaws lets an experienced pilot exploit each opponent's particular weaknesses; it also stays responsive at all speeds. Against that, its top speed is low, its armament ordinary and its ammunition supply small. It was added in Update 1.43.
yak-23: The Yak-23 continued the Yak-15/17 line, still built on the Yak-3's airframe but powered by the Klimov RD-500 turbojet; less successful than the MiG-9 yet produced in reasonable numbers, 319 were built and served with Poland, Romania, Albania, Bulgaria, North Korea and Czechoslovakia. In the game it is an oddity among jets like the MiG-15bis and A-4E: its prop-style airframe turns well at moderate speed, but it compresses badly when fast and has no airbrake. A strong, quick-accelerating engine lets it hold around 700-800 km/h, the sweet spot for turning, and its guns are effective once their ballistics are learned. It arrived in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
yak-28b: Probably the last Yakovlev combat jet to enter Soviet service and the first Soviet supersonic frontline bomber, the Yak-28 derived from the Yak-26 and was built in Irkutsk from 1960 to 1971; the Yak-28B was an early tactical bomber version with Lotos radar, though the Yak-28P interceptor was the most numerous. In the game its payload is barely better than some subsonic NATO attackers. Speed and 64 countermeasures let it decoy infrared missiles of its era, but with bomber handling and just 50 rounds of 23 mm it should not try to intercept, as fighters will shoot it down easily. It arrived in the "Red Skies" update.
yak-3: Developed from Yakovlev's I-30 prototype and refined with lessons from the Yak-1, the Yak-3 was built for minimal drag and size, entering service in July 1944 with the VK-105 since the intended VK-107 was not ready; 4,848 were produced and did well against German fighters, especially below 4,000 m. In the game it balances speed, agility and firepower and excels low down, where few opponents can match it below 2,000 m, and it can rival some Spitfires in turns with careful flap use. It gains and keeps energy easily, but climbing too high blunts its performance. It has been in the game since the open beta before Update 1.27.
yak-30d: Yakovlev's Yak-30 was a fresh swept-wing design derived from the experimental Yak-25, intended to challenge Mikoyan-Gurevich once the Yak-3-based jets had achieved little; the first version, flown in 1948, disappointed, and the improved Yak-30D tested well but lost out to the MiG-15, already in production. In the game it plays in much the same way as the MiG-15 and La-15, at its best around 800-900 km/h and able to pass 1,000 km/h at sea level on fuel-hungry 112% thrust. Above 850 km/h it bleeds energy in manoeuvres and compresses, so it should slow down before dogfighting, which its airbrake makes easy. It arrived in Update 1.59 "Flaming Arrows".
yak-38: Built for the Navy's Project 1143 carriers after the failed Yak-36 secured funding for a Soviet VTOL programme, the Yak-38 was a simpler, subsonic alternative to Yakovlev's Harrier-style supersonic proposal; it first flew in September 1970 but needed six years of fixes before entering service in 1976. In the game it can hover, unlike conventional jets, yet like the Yak-38M it flies poorly. Its weapons make up for this: R-60 missiles, rocket pods, bombs, gun pods and Kh-23M guided missiles. Sold as a premium pack from the "New Power" update, it was withdrawn after the 2022 Summer sale and returned for Golden Eagles in September 2023.
yak-38m: Overheating, weak and heavy engines left the early Yak-38 well behind the Harrier, so the Navy asked for an upgrade; the resulting Yak-38M, in service from 1985, had new R-28V-300 and RD-38 engines, upgraded avionics, better guidance and autopilot and all-aspect R-60 missiles. In the game this VTOL strike aircraft is almost indistinguishable from the Yak-38 apart from a longer, red-painted tail boom and a striped pitot tube. Flight performance is underwhelming, but strong armament and ordnance options compensate, and it leads on to the far more capable Yak-141. It arrived in the "New Power" update.
yak-3_eremin: Only 197 early Yak-3s carried the single 20 mm ShVAK and 12.7 mm UBS, and one of them was presented in May 1944 by collective farmer Ferapont Golovaty to pilot Boris Eremin, who had already scored eight victories in a Yak-1B paid for by Golovaty; Eremin downed six more in it and ended the war in Prague. In the game it is an excellent fighter up to 5,000 m, but ammunition is limited, the guns are weak and the structural speed limit is low, while its water-cooled engine and modest toughness make any hit dangerous. It was a 2024 "Legend of Victory" event reward.
yak-3_france: France's Normandie-Niemen squadron, formed in 1942 and sent to the Eastern Front, claimed more than 200 victories flying Yaks and ended the war on the Yak-3, which it kept flying afterwards until shortages of spare parts grounded the fleet; the unit still exists and now flies Rafales. In the game this premium is a dangerous fighter with excellent handling, good energy retention in turns and a climb rate above 21 m/s. Power falls off above 5,000 m, and the wooden airframe's 685 km/h limit makes steep dives risky. It is a good aircraft for learning energy and dogfighting tactics. It arrived in Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm".
yak-3_vk107: This experimental Yak-3 adapted the airframe to the more powerful VK-107, moving the cockpit 400 mm back, enlarging fuel and oil tanks and strengthening the undercarriage; despite engine reliability problems it reached 720 km/h at 5,750 m, a Soviet record, and passed state trials in August 1944, but work ended in 1946 after 48 all-metal examples. In the game it climbs exceptionally well and is fast at every altitude while keeping most of the VK-105 Yak-3's agility, making it a superb energy fighter. Light armament and a low maximum permitted speed stop it from fully exploiting that performance. It arrived in Update 1.51 "Cold Steel".
yak-3p: The Yak-3P, the most common Yak-3, replaced the earlier mix of guns with three 20 mm Berezin B-20 cannons that weighed less yet delivered a heavier burst than most rivals; production began after the war, and none of the 596 built saw combat. In the game it is among the strongest fighters at its rank, combining excellent agility, high speed and cannons that can wreck an aircraft with a single hit. Like other Yaks it fades above 3,000 m, and its wooden wing tips and control stiffening beyond 600 km/h make high-speed dives unwise. It arrived in Update 1.35.
yak-3t: Converted at the Yakovlev bureau between December 1944 and January 1945, the Yak-3T gave the light Yak-3 Yak-9T-class firepower, a 37 mm N-37 cannon and two 20 mm B-20S in place of the ShVAK and UBS guns, at a small cost in weight and handling. Trials went well, but the war's end and an unreliable engine unit kept it out of production. In the game it flies much like the Yak-3, very agile at low and medium altitude, and its heavy guns win head-on passes. It keeps the base model's low dive limit and small ammunition supply. It was a 2017 "Chronicles of World War II" reward.
yak-3u: The Yak-3U swapped the Yak-3's inline engine for an ASh-82FN radial, replacing many wooden and fabric parts with duralumin, enlarging the wing and moving it forward, and raising the cockpit for visibility; the prototype was finished in April 1945 and later given an all-metal wing, but with the war over the need for it vanished. In the game it combines excellent manoeuvrability with strong acceleration and flight performance, though these advantages fade quickly above 4 km, and its maximum permitted speed is low. It arrived in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy".
yak-4: Created in 1940 by re-engining the BB-22 (Yak-2) with Klimov VK-105s, the Yak-4 light reconnaissance bomber entered production at Moscow's Plant No. 81 that October; poor build quality and a small bomb load brought heavy losses early in the war, and only 90 were built before production stopped in 1941. In the game it is fast, climbs decently and handles well, making it a reasonable light bomber in air and combined battles. Its engines overheat quickly, though, and the turret and 8 mm armour plate do little to protect aircraft or crew. It arrived in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
yak-7b: Originally a two-seat trainer for the Yak-1 family, the Yak-7 was reworked into a single-seat fighter that kept the rear compartment; the Yak-7B, with a shorter wingspan, better equipment and easier-to-build undercarriage, was the most numerous version at around 5,000 aircraft. In the game it is less agile than other Yaks but still competitive, climbing well even without WEP and performing respectably at altitude. Ammunition is limited and the wings tear off in steep dives, so short bursts and gentle dive exits matter, and staying near allies helps when pursued. It has been in the game since the open beta before Update 1.27.
yak-9: Developed alongside the Yak-3 and drawing on Yak-7 combat experience, the mixed wood-and-metal Yak-9 became the most important Soviet fighter family, entering service in October 1942 and spawning night fighter, long-range, anti-tank and escort variants; the base model carried a 20 mm ShVAK and a 12.7 mm UB. In the game it is a well-rounded fighter with no glaring weakness, though its wooden wings rule out steep dives and long turning fights gradually drain its energy. Ammunition is limited, but nose-mounted guns need no convergence adjustment, which makes hitting targets easier. It arrived in Update 1.43.
yak-9b: A fighter-bomber offshoot of the long-range Yak-9D, the Yak-9B had four vertical bomb tubes behind the cockpit for up to four 100 kg bombs or PTAB cluster cassettes, though 200 kg was the usual load. Poor handling when loaded and no bomb sight kept it from mass production. In the game it is the only Yak with an internal bomb bay, letting it strike ground targets and still fight for air superiority, which suits ground realistic battles. It flies like other Yaks, best at low altitude, with slightly reduced agility when carrying bombs. It arrived in Update 1.53 "Firestorm".
yak-9k: The Yak-9K tried to outgun the Yak-9T with a 45 mm NS-45 cannon carrying 29 rounds and a muzzle brake, but below 350 km/h the recoil could throw the aircraft off course and jolt the pilot, firing caused oil and coolant leaks, and performance suffered, especially at altitude, so it saw only limited use with Yak-3 escorts. In the game a single hit can cripple any aircraft, and the gun can also be used against tanks in ground battles, but heavy recoil unsettles the airframe and with just 29 rounds every shot must count. It arrived in Update 1.33.
yak-9m: This Yak-9M wears the colours of Pavel Golovachev, who flew the type with the 900th fighter squadron in 1945, including during the Battle of Berlin; no other Yak-9M appears in the game, and it carries pre-applied decals and fuselage lettering. Its nose-mounted 20 mm cannon and 12.7 mm Berezin are effective by Soviet standards at its tier but modest against other nations. Climbing to about 2,000 m gives it enough energy to engage, and while flaps make it a decent turner, it loses energy quickly in horizontal fights. First sold as a pack in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory", it has returned in occasional sales.
yak-9p: The Yak-9P was a refined postwar Yak-9 with an all-metal airframe, extra fuel tanks and a choice of armament, its polished silver finish inviting comparison with the P-51D. In the game the extra weight leaves it flying about the same as, or slightly worse than, the Yak-9U, but it still blends speed and agility well. Flown carefully, its balanced performance and heavy firepower make it a dangerous opponent. It arrived in Update 1.31.
yak-9p_hungary: Developed from the Yak-9U with an all-metal skin as postwar priorities shifted from quantity to quality, the Yak-9P was adopted by the Soviet Air Force in 1947; about 120 went to Hungary in the late 1940s, serving with the 25th and 66th Fighter Aviation Divisions until MiG-15s replaced them by the end of 1954. This Italian-tree example differs from the Soviet one only in its Hungarian camouflage. It has strong guns and good agility, but high-altitude speed is mediocre, the engine overheats quickly and handling stiffens above 500 km/h, making it a middleweight that can adapt to most opponents. It arrived in Update 2.35 "Alpha Strike".
yak-9t: The Yak-9T traded the ShVAK for a 37 mm NS-37 with 30 rounds, moving the cockpit 0.4 m aft to balance the heavier nose; 2,748 were built from 1943 to 1945 and used against Black Sea shipping and armour on several fronts, while a single hit could also break up an aircraft. In the game its armour-piercing rounds readily penetrate tank roofs in a dive, and the Yak-9's strong low-altitude performance makes it an excellent close-support aircraft. With only 30 rounds, aim must be precise, and short bursts avoid overheating the barrel and losing accuracy. It has been in the game since the open beta before Update 1.27.
yak-9t_france: White 60 was the Yak-9T of René Challe, who escaped occupied France through Spain in 1943 and joined the Normandie-Niemen regiment, scoring eight confirmed victories before being badly wounded on 17 January 1945; he survived the war and died in 2006. In the game the 37 mm NS-37 rewards Challe's method of closing to around 100 m and waiting for the target to show a broad surface, as the slow reload and small ammunition load leave no room for spraying. It can also dive on tank roofs with AP shells. It came in Update 1.73 "Vive la France" and was briefly sold for Golden Eagles in 2017.
yak-9u: Based on the Yak-9T with Yak-3-style aerodynamic and structural refinements, the Yak-9U used the 1,650 hp VK-107A, and its 700 km/h at 5,600 m was bettered among production fighters of the time only by the P-51B; widened radiators solved early overheating, and no Soviet fighter of the time performed better at altitude. In the game it is one of the few Yaks comfortable up high, keeping good performance to 5,000 m, and one of the quickest aircraft in its class near the ground. Speed, acceleration, climb and agility are all impressive, but its armament is mediocre for its level. It arrived in Update 1.37.
yak-9ut: Concerned that Yak guns lacked punch, Soviet designers rearmed the Yak-9U from late 1944 with two 20 mm B-20S cannons and a hub cannon of 23, 37 or 45 mm; it entered production with the 23 mm gun, and 282 were built between February and May 1945, some fighting in the war's last weeks. In the game it flies much like the Yak-9U, agile and reasonably fast at low and medium altitude, though its dive limit is low. The real difference is firepower: two 20 mm guns plus a choice of 23, 37 or 45 mm cannon, enough to destroy aircraft or tanks. It arrived in Update 1.37.
yak_130_early: The Yak-130 ("Mitten") is a two-seat advanced jet trainer that can also fly light combat missions, developed from the early 1990s to replace the L-39ZA; Aermacchi joined in 1993 but left after disagreements and used the work for its M-346, while Yakovlev finished the Yak-130 alone. Chosen over the MiG-AT in 2002, it entered Russian service in 2010. In the game it handles well and carries TV-guided bombs, but its top speed is low and it has no countermeasures, so IR missiles can only be decoyed by firing an S-25OFM rocket, and SARH missiles must be out-manoeuvred. It arrived in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
yak_141: The Yak-141 ("Freestyle") was a supersonic VTOL fighter prototype intended to replace the Yak-38: far larger and more refined, with a very powerful Tumansky R-79 main engine, up-to-date avionics and long-range weapons, it was set to give the Soviet Navy a world-class carrier fighter until the collapse of the USSR stopped it. In the game it is a fully fledged fourth-generation fighter comparable to the MiG-29. It lacks Mach 2 speed but turns surprisingly well and accelerates superbly, and R-27ER missiles with a 70 km radar make it lethal at every range. It arrived in the "Sky Guardians" update.
yak_1_litvyak: Lydia Litvyak, the most successful female fighter pilot of the war, talked her way into the Red Army in 1941 and flew Yak-1s with the 586th and then the 437th Fighter Aviation Regiments, scoring her first solo kill in September 1942 and many more in 1943 before going missing on 1 August 1943; her tally is disputed. In the game her Yak-1 has a better engine than the standard model and is otherwise the same balanced fighter, able to beat rivals on either speed or agility. It climbs slowly, and handling and power suffer at altitude. It arrived in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
yak_2_kabb: Built for light bombing and reconnaissance, the Yak-2 (originally Ya-22) was rushed into service as Germany invaded; the KABB conversion, named for designers Mozharovsky and Venevidov, removed the radio operator-gunner to make room for four 100 kg bombs, gave the pilot a fully glazed nose and added a ventral pack with two 20 mm cannons and two 7.62 mm guns aligned with the fuselage. In the game it can intercept from altitude with boom-and-zoom attacks or outrun fighters that climb to meet it. Low down it is an effective attacker, bombing vehicles and AA guns, then strafing once the bombs are gone. It arrived in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
yp-38: Ordered as a pre-production P-38 once the sole XP-38 had been lost, the YP-38 was lighter, had outward-turning propellers that steadied gun firing and was meant to carry four machine guns and a 37 mm cannon in the nose; delivered from late 1940, it suffered in high-speed dives, one breaking up and killing its pilot. In the game the nose guns are accurate but short of ammunition, and it climbs well and handles nicely around 500 km/h, but it overspeeds easily, stiffens when fast and carries no bombs or rockets. A premium from the "Raining Fire" update, where it replaced the XP-38G, it left the store in 2023.
z_10: After watching AH-64s destroy Iraqi armour in the Gulf War, the PLA set out to build a dedicated attack helicopter, consulting Kamov on the early design from 1995 before largely redeveloping it; the Z-10 joined the army in 2009 with an exceptional combat radius. In the game it is China's first full attack helicopter, with armour, an internal gun and the full-size AKD-10, a laser-guided missile that hits tanks hard. Its early WZ-9 engines are underpowered, though, so it is agile but not especially quick, it carries fewer ATGMs than comparable helicopters, and there is no mast radar like the Z-19's. It arrived in the "Drone Age" update.
z_1007_bis_serie3: The CANT Z.1007 bis "Alcione" ("Kingfisher") was a wooden tri-motor medium bomber designed under Filippo Zappata, first flown in March 1937 and in service from May 1939; production Serie III aircraft used more powerful Piaggio P.XI RC.40 engines and had dorsal and ventral turrets with heavy machine guns. In the game its turrets give solid defensive fire and it carries a respectable bomb load, but it is slow and does not absorb much damage. It arrived in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
z_1007_bis_serie5: Set apart from the serie 3 by a twin tail and a fractionally higher top speed, this version of the CANT tri-motor medium bomber improves on the SM.79 in every respect in the game: it can carry two internal 500 kg bombs plus six external 100 kg, six 250 kg bombs, or a torpedo, covering targets from bases and tanks to ships. Three engines give decent performance, but losing one hurts badly. Speed is its main defence, since the dorsal turret has only a single 12.7 mm gun, the 7.7 mm waist guns are nearly useless and the ventral gun covers little. It arrived in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
z_10a: From the late 2010s, Chinese Z-10s were brought up to Z-10A standard, fixing prototype shortcomings and adding cockpit armour, better fire control and electro-optics and stronger engines; with more than 200 in service, it is now China's main attack helicopter. In the game it differs from the Z-10 through armour around the cockpit and engines and slightly more power, and otherwise plays the same: not especially fast but agile, with capable AKD-10 anti-tank missiles and very good TY-90 air-to-air missiles. It carries few countermeasures and little ammunition for its 23 mm cannon. It arrived in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
z_10me: Unveiled at Zhuhai in 2016, the Z-10ME is the export Z-10, refined over several versions with stronger engines, more cannon ammunition, upturned exhausts, Kevlar crew panels and, by 2024, engine armour, a mast radar, IRCM and missile approach warning; Pakistan ordered 40 in 2022 after its T-129 deal collapsed. In the game its AKD-10 anti-tank missiles are among the weakest of its peers, being slow, lofted and needing constant laser guidance, but agile, flare-resistant TY-90s make it a flying air-defence battery, and the radar eases target finding. Its small armour panels stop little, though missile warning and IRCM help. It arrived in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
z_11wa: The Changhe Z-11, China's first domestically designed helicopter, was developed from 1991 using the AS.350 Écureuil as a basis, flying in 1994 and entering production in 1998; the Z-11WA reconnaissance version with improved sighting systems followed in 2004. In the game it is quick, small and very agile, with thermal imaging and HJ-8A ATGMs, but its weapon choice is narrow: slow, short-ranged HJ-8As, rocket pods of 57 and 90 mm, and 12.7 mm gun pods. With no armour or other protection, it works best by spotting targets from afar and sneaking in to strike from unexpected directions. It arrived in the "Drone Age" update.
z_19: Derived from the Z-9WA, itself based on the licence-built Dauphin, the Z-19 "Black Whirlwind" is an army observation and attack helicopter with a tandem cockpit, millimetre-wave radar and modern Chinese electronics; it first flew in 2011, entered service in 2012, and more than 150 have been delivered. In the game it turns the Dauphin into a true attack helicopter, swapping HJ-8 SACLOS missiles for Hellfire-like AKD-9 laser-guided ones, doubling hardpoints to eight and adding a mast radar and auto-tracker. It threatens both tanks and aircraft, but protection is light and it has no internal gun. It arrived in the "Drone Age" update.
z_19e: Shown as a mock-up at Zhuhai in 2016 and flown in 2017, the export Z-19E uses more composites to cut noise and weight and has new engines; Pakistan was a likely buyer, but the project's fate is unknown. In the game it flies superbly and can manage aerobatics most rivals cannot. BA-9 laser-guided ATGMs act as lighter, shorter-ranged Hellfires backed by excellent thermal optics, while countermeasures and missile warning make it hard to bring down. Its standout weapon is the TY-90, an agile, flare-resistant all-aspect missile with a 6 km lock range; carrying up to eight, it can fight for air superiority. It arrived in the "Danger Zone" update.
z_9w: The Z-9W "Haitun" ("Dolphin") was an armed version of the Harbin Z-9, China's licence-built AS365 Dauphin, and one of the PLA army aviation's first dedicated attack helicopters, adding door hardpoints and roof-mounted sights for guiding ATGMs. In the game it is a comfortable step up from the Z-11WA: the Dauphin airframe is very agile and aerobatic, and it brings a high-zoom camera, a ballistic computer, improved HJ-8C missiles and 23 mm cannons. It also introduces TY-90 air-to-air missiles, letting it double as a flying SPAA, so it can work against ground targets, enemy helicopters or both. It arrived in the "Drone Age" update.
z_9wa: Developed in 2005, the Z-9WA upgraded the Z-9W with a thermal-imaging sight, better avionics and compatibility with newer weapons, and was exported as well as serving in China. In the game it stays fast and light, but as a converted transport design it can lag behind its peers; it compensates by carrying more of its better ATGMs and air-to-air missiles. Thermal optics, missile approach warning and countermeasures make it a better tank hunter than the Z-9W and harder for air defences to catch. It arrived in the "Drone Age" update.
